SN-15.title: Bakel, Dry Hills
SN-15.description: Dry terrain with gentle hills appears around Bakel and south to Nayé.

s_general_01_06.title: French colonial influence
s_general_01_06.description: In Senegal, French is the official language and dominates all visible signage.

CA-5.title: Centre Line Markings
CA-5.description: Canadian roads commonly use a single yellow centre line; double yellow lines also appear.

sun-to-south.title: Sun visible to the south
sun-to-south.description: The sun appears toward the south, which usually points to a northern-hemisphere location.

GB-5.title: Wooden Poles with Steps
GB-5.description: Timber utility poles have thin horizontal metal rungs bolted up one side.

OM-10.title: Wooden Utility Poles
OM-10.description: Wooden power poles in Oman have three distinct top designs, including a unique metal triangle above one variant.

OM-4.title: Arabic
OM-4.description: Arabic is Oman's sole official language; signage often appears in Arabic and English.

OM-5.title: Yellow Edge Lines with White Centre Lines
OM-5.description: Omani roads have yellow lines along edges and white lines down the centre.

OM-6.title: Black-and-Yellow Curbs
OM-6.description: Kerbs painted in alternating black and yellow segments are widespread on Omani roads.

OM-7.title: Light Stone Architecture with Ornate Fences
OM-7.description: Omani homes are pale stone with decorative details, enclosed by matching stone fences with elaborate gates.

o_general_01.title: Desert landscape
o_general_01.description: Oman is dominated by arid, sparsely vegetated terrain. The central and southern interior is largely flat, while the northern coastline has dry, rugged mountains

ID-22.title: Satellite Dish Direction
ID-22.description: Satellite dishes aim towards the equator; dish direction indicates relative position to it.

ID-3.title: Utility Poles
ID-3.description: Cylindrical steel or concrete poles, some painted black with red-and-white bands. Crossbars may be symmetrical or asymmetrical.

ID-31.title: Clay Tile Roofs on Java
ID-31.description: Terracotta roof tiles are mainly a Javanese feature.

ID-41.title: Regional Licence Plate Codes
ID-41.description: Plate prefixes indicate region: single letters on western Java, two letters on eastern Java and other islands.

sun-overhead.title: Sun visible overhead
sun-overhead.description: The sun appears high overhead, which usually points to a location near the tropics.

BR-24.title: Rio Grande do Sul
BR-24.description: Landscape alternates between rolling hills and flat green pastures.

BR-27.title: Paraná Pines
BR-27.description: Araucaria trees have long horizontal branches with foliage clustered at tips, found in Paraná, Santa Catarina, and Rio Grande do Sul.

BR-80.title: European-Influenced Architecture
BR-80.description: Southern states, especially Santa Catarina, feature buildings with Germanic architectural style.

BR-9.title: Orange Roof Tiles
BR-9.description: Terracotta-orange clay tiles are standard roofing material nationwide.

sun-to-north.title: Sun visible to the north
sun-to-north.description: The sun appears toward the north, which usually points to a southern-hemisphere location.

drives-on-right.title: Vehicles drive on the right
drives-on-right.description: Traffic here appears to drive on the right side of the road.

AU-0.title: Gum Trees (Eucalyptus)
AU-0.description: Eucalyptus trees have pale bark and rounded clumps of foliage.

AU-17.title: Upward-Angled Coil Pole Tops
AU-17.description: Queensland electricity poles often have side-mounted coils that tilt upwards.

AU-24.title: Short Bollard Reflectors
AU-24.description: Bollards with reflectors shorter than standard are concentrated in Queensland and South Australia.

AU-51.title: Tropical North Queensland
AU-51.description: Far north Queensland's coastal strip is lushly tropical with palms and dense dark green foliage.

AU-52.title: Sugarcane Fields
AU-52.description: Sugarcane fields dominate northern Queensland's tropical agricultural landscape.

AU-6.title: Chevrons
AU-6.description: Curve warning chevrons appear as white arrows on black or black arrows on yellow.

au_bollards_01.title: Bollards
au_bollards_01.description: Australian bollards are white with a vertical red stripe towards the top.

drives-on-left.title: Vehicles drive on the left
drives-on-left.description: Traffic here appears to drive on the left side of the road.

JP-12.title: White Guardrails
JP-12.description: Plain white guardrails are the default road barrier throughout Japan.

JP-15.title: Retaining Walls
JP-15.description: Retaining walls in remote countryside indicate you are in Japan.

JP-3.title: Japanese Writing Systems
JP-3.description: Japanese uses kanji, hiragana with rounded strokes, and angular katakana scripts.

JP-6.title: Architecture
JP-6.description: Building styles range from traditional rural houses to ultramodern urban high-rises.

JP-7.title: Round Concrete Poles
JP-7.description: Utility poles are round concrete with threaded screw-like protrusions and often electrical plates.

jp_road_01.title: Driving direction
jp_road_01.description: In Japan they drive on the left side of the road.

jp_vehicles_01.title: Boxy cars
jp_vehicles_01.description: In Japan small, boxy cars are very common. They are called Kei cars.

RU-82.title: Summer Coverage
RU-82.description: Summer coverage is the most common and widespread.

KE-13.title: Regional Climates
KE-13.description: Kenya spans humid to very arid climate zones; use climate as a regional clue.

ke_vehicles_01.title: Grey Pickup Truck
ke_vehicles_01.description: In a lot of the Kenyan coverage, you can see the large grey Street View pickup truck, sometimes with a black snorkel.

ID-32.title: Corrugated Metal Roofs
ID-32.description: Sheet-metal roofing predominates in northern and outer islands like Kalimantan, Sulawesi, and Sumatra.

EC-23.title: Esmeraldas Province
EC-23.description: Esmeraldas has Amazon-like vegetation but is hillier.

EC-8.title: Chevron Overuse
EC-8.description: Road bends have a high density of chevron signs.

MY-flag.title: Country Flag
MY-flag.description: The national flag of Malaysia is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

DE-2.title: German Language
DE-2.description: Signs are in German, identifiable by Ä, Ö, Ü, and ß characters.

DE-31.title: Northwestern Brick Houses
DE-31.description: Exposed red or brown brick houses concentrate in the northwest.

DE-5.title: Dark Sign Backs
DE-5.description: Road sign backs are often black or dark grey, with a small inverted red triangle sticker on most signs.

DE-6.title: Yellow 'H' Bus Stops
DE-6.description: Bus stops feature a yellow-and-green 'H' symbol.

d_general_01_08.title: German bollard
d_general_01_08.description: German bollards are black-and-white posts fitted with white or pale grey reflectors, switching to orange at intersections.

AR-5.title: Road Lines
AR-5.description: Roads have broken white centre lines, solid double yellow dividers, or both.

xx_general_01_57.title: Argentina chevrons
xx_general_01_57.description: Argentina is the only South American country that has white chevrons with red arrows.

r_general_01_02.title: Cyrillic script
r_general_01_02.description: Russian uses the Cyrillic alphabet. It is the only script showing up on most signs.

US-52.title: Douglas Firs in Cascadia
US-52.description: Extremely tall conifers with dark brown bark and dark green foliage, common in Washington and Oregon.

US-71.title: Brown National Park Infrastructure
US-71.description: Guardrails, signs, and sign posts painted medium brown are characteristic of US national parks. Rock walls sometimes replace guardrails.

US-21.title: Wooden Utility Poles
US-21.description: North America predominantly uses wooden utility poles.

US-25.title: Water Towers
US-25.description: Tall water towers are common in US and Canadian towns, often displaying town or state names.

US-50.title: Sagebrush
US-50.description: Great Basin sagebrush is a short, shrubby blue-green bush common in arid interior western US.

CO-13.title: Afro-Colombian Pacific Coast
CO-13.description: The Pacific coastline has a predominantly Afro-Colombian population.

CO-7.title: Concrete and Dark Poles
CO-7.description: Most poles are concrete, with dark-coloured poles more common here than nearby countries.

co_vehicles_01_01.title: Yellow plates
co_vehicles_01_01.description: Colombia is the only country in South America that uses all yellow license plates for personal vehicles.

xx_misc_01_08.title: Rickety fences
xx_misc_01_08.description: It is common to find wooden fences in Colombia, often made from various pieces of wood.

xx_pole_01_04.title: Painted poles
xx_pole_01_04.description: Colombian poles can be found painted with black-yellow-black stripes.

xx_general_01_61.title: Mailboxes
xx_general_01_61.description: Mailboxes with a small flag are a common sight in North America.

KE-7.title: County Names on Signage
KE-7.description: Signs often display Kenyan county names, useful for regional identification.

xx_general_01_45.title: Mobile network
xx_general_01_45.description: The mobile network Safaricom is exclusive to Kenya, and its branded signage appears in almost every town.

KZ-6.title: Blue Street Signs on Buildings
KZ-6.description: Kazakh street signs are blue with white patterns, mounted on building facades, often bilingual or trilingual.

xx_general_01_46.title: Tree trunks
xx_general_01_46.description: The bottom of tree trunks in Kazakhstan are often painted white.

BR-7.title: Road Markings
BR-7.description: Centre lines are typically double solid yellow; edge lines are white.

ID-9.title: Front Licence Plates on Motorcycles
ID-9.description: Indonesian motorcycles carry a front licence plate, unlike other Southeast Asian countries.

US-135.title: Sheetz
US-135.description: Sheetz is a gas station and convenience store chain in the Eastern US, concentrated in the Mid-Atlantic and Central Appalachia.

US-19.title: Overhead Traffic Light Bars
US-19.description: Long metal arms with traffic lights, street signs, and highway signs extend over intersections throughout the US and Canada.

u_general_01_04.title: Road lines
u_general_01_04.description: US roads have yellow center lines (usually double) and white outer lines.

us_road-signs_02.title: Yield signs
us_road-signs_02.description: US yield signs are triangles with a red border and the word “YIELD” on a white background.

DE-4.title: Diverse Pole Tops
DE-4.description: Common German pole tops include horizontal crossarms with staggered insulators, inverted-triangle supports, and T-shaped arrangements.

RO-0.title: Licence Plates
RO-0.description: Romanian plates are long, white European style with a single blue strip on the left.

RO-1.title: Romanian Language
RO-1.description: A Romance language with unique diacritics Ă/ă, Ș/ș, and Ț/ț.

RO-flag.title: Country Flag
RO-flag.description: The national flag of Romania is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

xx_general_01_32.title: Holey poles
xx_general_01_32.description: In Romania, you will frequently come across so called holey poles, with holes running all the way down to the ground.

AR-10.title: Western Mountains
AR-10.description: The far west is dominated by mountainous terrain along the Andes.

AR-17.title: Tierra del Fuego Grass
AR-17.description: Low, windswept grass with few shrubs signals Tierra del Fuego or SE Santa Cruz.

AR-3.title: Wooden Utility Poles
AR-3.description: Timber poles appear frequently, including unique A-frame variants.

AR-8.title: Wide Open Landscape
AR-8.description: Vast, open terrain with sparse vegetation and few people.

JP-10.title: Road Lines
JP-10.description: Japanese road markings include solid white edges with dashed or solid white/yellow center lines.

JP-18.title: Regional Pole Reflector Pads
JP-18.description: Reflector pads on utility poles vary in design by region.

JP-66.title: Cabbage
JP-66.description: Cabbage grows prolifically in Hokkaido and parts of northern Honshu, often visible beside roads.

JP-73.title: Hokkaido Winter Coverage
JP-73.description: Snowy winter Google Street View is scarce in Hokkaido, mostly in the southern part.

j_general_01_02.title: Overhead arrows
j_general_01_02.description: This arrow above the road marks the road during heavy snow and is mainly seen in Hokkaido.

jp_pole_01.title: Pole markings
jp_pole_01.description: Japanese poles often have thin, vertical yellow lines on a black section towards the bottom.

AT-0.title: Licence Plates
AT-0.description: Austrian licence plates are elongated and white, featuring the blue EU band on the left edge.

AT-17.title: Anfang/Ende Signs
AT-17.description: Parking restriction signs often include 'Anfang' (start) or 'Ende' (end) to mark zone boundaries.

AT-20.title: Mountainous south
AT-20.description: The centre and west are mountainous, while the east and north are flatter, with rolling hills.

AT-27.title: Vorarlberg White Km Markers
AT-27.description: White kilometre markers appear in Vorarlberg and western Salzburg.

AT-33.title: Highest Alps
AT-33.description: Austria's highest Alpine peaks cluster near the Italian border in the west.

AT-4.title: Landscape
AT-4.description: Most of Austria is forested mountain terrain, with eastern regions flattening into agricultural lowlands.

AT-5.title: Alpine Architecture
AT-5.description: Traditional Alpine homes have pale walls, wooden balconies, and wide overhanging dark timber roofs.

AT-6.title: German Language
AT-6.description: Austria's official language is German, recognizable by characters Ä, Ö, Ü, and ß.

xx_bollards_01_04.title: Black top bollards
xx_bollards_01_04.description: Austrian roadside bollards are white with a black cap, often with a small rounded knob at the very top.

US-20.title: Thin Metal Sign Posts
US-20.description: Thin metal sign posts, either perforated or U-shaped, are standard in North America.

ZA-27.title: Dry Northeast Landscape
ZA-27.description: Arid terrain with orange-red soil and shrub-covered hills or mountains characterises the northeast.

ZA-5.title: Bird Poles
ZA-5.description: South African poles often have 1–5 horizontal bars with thin white insulators resembling rows of perching birds.

ZA-7.title: Triangular Warning Signs
ZA-7.description: South African warning signs are red-bordered triangles on a white background.

xx_general_01_18.title: South African chevrons
xx_general_01_18.description: South Africa uses red and white chevron signs, and small, thin chevrons with a single arrow are common across Southern African countries.

z_general_01_01.title: High security
z_general_01_01.description: In South Africa, suburban homes in and around major cities are commonly enclosed behind tall walls, fences, and gates.

BR-10.title: Transparent Satellite Dishes
BR-10.description: Clear or translucent satellite dishes on rooftops are common and unique in Latin America.

BR-25.title: Southeastern Rolling Hills
BR-25.description: Minas Gerais, Rio de Janeiro, and Espírito Santo have gentle grass-covered rolling hills.

BR-26.title: Exposed Rock Mountains
BR-26.description: Tall mountains with bare rock faces are common in Espírito Santo and nearby regions.

br_nature_01.title: Red soil
br_nature_01.description: This iron rich, red soil is primarily found in Brazil.

JP-69.title: Japanese White Birch
JP-69.description: This tree species is concentrated in Chubu and Hokkaido, with some presence in Tohoku.

NO-1.title: Wooden Houses
NO-1.description: Norwegian homes are mostly wooden, often red-painted; black-painted houses are more common here than in neighbors.

LK-21.title: Wet Southwest Climate
LK-21.description: The southwest receives more rainfall, producing dense, deep-green vegetation.

xx_general_01_43.title: Sri Lanka poles
xx_general_01_43.description: Sri Lanka commonly uses concrete utility poles with large see through holes in the lower half, often called holey poles

EE-17.title: Architecture
EE-17.description: Estonian buildings combine wooden cladding, white-rendered brick, and steep corrugated metal roofs.

EE-6.title: Short-Dash Edge Lines
EE-6.description: Road edge markings sometimes use unusually short dashes.

PL-13.title: Tree-Lined Roads
PL-13.description: Rows of mature trees flanking both sides of roads are common across Poland.

PL-15.title: Architecture
PL-15.description: Central European style with plain stone walls, pastel stucco, and orange, red, black, or brown roof tiles; detached homes and communist-era blocks.

US-49-nevada.title: Nevada Great Basin
US-49-nevada.description: Vast, arid plains with low shrubs and isolated mountain ranges, often snow-capped in winter and spring.

US-54.title: Southwest Mesas and Red Rock
US-54.description: The Four Corners region features mesas, tablelands, and reddish rock formations with red soil.

US-55.title: Palm Trees
US-55.description: Common along the Southeast coast, Gulf Coast, and Desert Southwest; Mexican Fan Palm prevalent in California.

NO-29.title: Spruce Trees
NO-29.description: Spruce trees are concentrated in the southern half of Norway, especially in the southeast and Trondheim region.

n_general_01_09.title: Directional signs
n_general_01_09.description: In Norway directional signs are yellow with a thin black outline.

BR-0.title: Licence Plates
BR-0.description: Pre-2018 plates were plain white; current plates have a blue strip on top; commercial plates are red.

xx_general_01_58.title: Black signs
xx_general_01_58.description: Most road signs in Brazil have black backsides.

US-flag.title: Country Flag
US-flag.description: The national flag of the United States is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

AT-3.title: Wooden Poles
AT-3.description: The predominant utility pole across Austria is a rounded timber design.

VN-24.title: Flat Agricultural Deltas
VN-24.description: Wide open, flat agricultural fields are most common in the Red River Delta and less so in the Mekong Delta.

VN-36.title: Mekong Delta, Low Single-Storey Houses
VN-36.description: Mekong Delta houses are boxy concrete and almost always single ground-level storey.

VN-flag.title: Country Flag
VN-flag.description: The national flag of Vietnam is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

pe_road-signs_01.title: Striped signposts
pe_road-signs_01.description: Many signposts in Peru are square-shaped and painted in alternating black and white.

FR-46.title: Stone Pines
FR-46.description: Umbrella-shaped stone pines line many roads along the Mediterranean coast, sometimes as far north as Nantes.

PH-7.title: Red-on-White Chevron Signs
PH-7.description: Philippine road curve chevrons use red arrows on white backgrounds.

PH-9.title: Tricycles / Tuk-Tuks
PH-9.description: Motorised tricycles (tuk-tuks) are ubiquitous and often outnumber cars.

ph_road_01.title: Concrete roads
ph_road_01.description: Roads in the Philippines are often made of big concrete blocks.

CA-23.title: Transformer Orientation (BC & NB)
CA-23.description: Pole-mounted transformers in British Columbia and New Brunswick face the road; elsewhere they align with the wires.

CA-48.title: Western Mountains
CA-48.description: Major mountain ranges are concentrated in British Columbia, western Alberta, and parts of Yukon.

CA-57.title: Québec City–Windsor Corridor
CA-57.description: Canada's most populated zone, a flat green belt mixing farmland and woodland between Québec City and Windsor.

CA-60.title: Area Codes
CA-60.description: Canadian phone numbers start with a three-digit area code in the format XXX XXX XXXX.

ca_language_01.title: Speed signs
ca_language_01.description: Speed signs in Canada say ‘Maximum’. This word works in both English and French, the official languages of Canada.

IT-5.title: Architecture
IT-5.description: Pastel stone houses with terracotta roofs and outward-swinging bi-fold wooden shutters.

IT-flag.title: Country Flag
IT-flag.description: The national flag of Italy is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

i_general_01_11.title: Street names
i_general_01_11.description: The Italian word for street is 'Via'.

it_license-plates_01.title: Double stripes
it_license-plates_01.description: The Italian license plates will have a blue strip on both sides. The front plates are also shorter than usual.

PL-11.title: Polish Language
PL-11.description: A West Slavic language with unique diacritics like Ł, Ą, Ę, Ż, and Ń, and W replacing V.

PL-3.title: Double White Centre Lines
PL-3.description: All road markings are white in Poland. Double centre lines are extremely common.

TR-13.title: Ladder and Mesh Metal Poles
TR-13.description: Metal utility poles with ladder or mesh-grid patterns are widespread in Turkey.

TR-18.title: Varied Landscape Across Regions
TR-18.description: Turkey's terrain ranges from arid southeast plains to Mediterranean coasts and greener northern forests.

TR-26.title: Northeastern Treeless Grassland Valleys
TR-26.description: The northeast has open valleys of grass between rounded, treeless hills.

TR-6.title: Red-on-White Chevron Signs
TR-6.description: Turkish chevron signs are red arrows on a white background, often with a neon yellow border.

TR-9.title: Wide-Spaced Font on Direction Signs
TR-9.description: Turkish directional signs use a typeface with large gaps between letters.

xx_general_01_05.title: Grainy roads
xx_general_01_05.description: Many roads in Turkey have a grainy look from the mix of light and dark local stones used in the asphalt.

SE-18.title: Landscape Overview
SE-18.description: Sweden has boreal forests, farmlands, lakes, mountainous north and west, and flatter south and east.

SE-2.title: White Road Lines
SE-2.description: All road markings in Sweden are white.

xx_general_01_21.title: Short dashes
xx_general_01_21.description: In Sweden, the outer road lines often have short, white dashed markings.

xx_road-signs_01.title: Checkered signs
xx_road-signs_01.description: In Canada, T-intersection signs are diamond-shaped and have a distinctive checkered pattern.

BO-17.title: Altiplano
BO-17.description: A highland plateau with grasslands ranging from green to brown, often with clumpy tufted grass.

BO-8.title: Utility Poles
BO-8.description: Main poles are cylindrical concrete with pinholes or timber, with varied crossarm designs.

b_general_01_09.title: Red bricks
b_general_01_09.description: Buildings featuring big exposed red bricks is a common sight in Bolivia.

US-33.title: Topographic Overview
US-33.description: The western US has major mountain ranges and high plateaus; the east is lower with the Appalachians as the main highland.

US-49-california.title: California Great Basin
US-49-california.description: Dry, shrubby valleys and tall, often snow-capped mountain ranges in eastern California near the Sierra Nevada.

US-77.title: California Black Stripe Between Centre Lines
US-77.description: A black stripe can sometimes be seen between the two yellow centre lines on California roads.

NO-flag.title: Country Flag
NO-flag.description: The national flag of Norway is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

n_general_01_10.title: White signs
n_general_01_10.description: Regulatory traffic signs in Norway feature a red border on a white background.

FR-0.title: Licence Plates
FR-0.description: Modern French plates are white rectangles with blue bands on left and right edges.

FR-15.title: Road Sign Borders
FR-15.description: Regulatory signs have a red border with a narrow white outline; white sub-signs with black text often attached below.

FR-27.title: Architecture
FR-27.description: Typical French houses are stone, unpainted or pale pastel, with simple gable roofs of orange tiles or dark slate; urban terraced houses line roads.

FR-28.title: Blue House Numbers
FR-28.description: Address plaques are predominantly blue with serif typeface and ornate numerals.

FR-29.title: French Car Brands
FR-29.description: Peugeot, Renault, and Citroën make up roughly half of all vehicles on the road.

FR-51.title: Black Shingle Roofs
FR-51.description: Slate or dark shingle roofs dominate northwest of the Loire, near the Belgian border, south-centre, and the Pyrenees.

VN-26.title: Central Highlands Landscape
VN-26.description: The Central Highlands are hilly with distant mountains, red soil, and dry rolling farmland.

VN-3.title: Red-and-White Striped Signposts
VN-3.description: Vietnamese road sign posts are usually painted with red-and-white stripes.

PL-16.title: Roadside Christian Shrines
PL-16.description: Small roadside shrines and blue-white or yellow-white Catholic flags are frequent.

PL-6.title: White Prohibitory Signs
PL-6.description: Polish round prohibitory signs use a white background with a thicker red border.

PL-flag.title: Country Flag
PL-flag.description: The national flag of Poland is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

pl_road-signs_01.title: No zebra
pl_road-signs_01.description: Pedestrian crossing signs in Poland only features a horizontal line. No "zebra stripes" here.

IE-3.title: Diamond-Shaped Warning Signs
IE-3.description: Irish hazard warnings use yellow diamond-shaped boards, unique in Europe.

i_general_01_08.title: Irish plates
i_general_01_08.description: Irish license plates are white and have the standard EU blue strip on the left.

xx_language_01_07.title: Bilingual signs
xx_language_01_07.description: Irish road signs usually carry text in both English and Irish.

RU-16.title: Black-and-White Pole Shields
RU-16.description: Pole shields with alternating black and white stripes appear frequently along highways in European Russia.

RU-4.title: Bollard Types
RU-4.description: Russia has three main bollard styles: thin on a stick, black top with red reflector, and German-style.

RU-64.title: Mosques
RU-64.description: Mosques are most common in Muslim-majority areas: the North Caucasus republics, Tatarstan, and Bashkortostan.

CA-34.title: BC Concrete Barriers
CA-34.description: British Columbia favours solid concrete barriers over metal guardrails on highways.

NA-15.title: Arid Mountains in the West and South
NA-15.description: Western and southern Namibia have barren, dry mountains and rocky hills.

n_general_01_03.title: Desert landscape
n_general_01_03.description: Desert-like landscape dominates most of Namibia, although there are a few exceptions to this.

xx_vehicles_01_05.title: White truck
xx_vehicles_01_05.description: Namibian Street View coverage was captured using a white pickup truck equipped with a short front-mounted antenna that consistently tilts slightly to the left.

ID-24.title: Painted Fences on Sulawesi
ID-24.description: Roadside fences painted white with blue or red highlights are common on Sulawesi.

BR-33.title: Macaw Palms
BR-33.description: Narrow-leaved palms with pointed spear-shaped crowns, common around Mato Grosso do Sul.

BR-8.title: White-Painted Kerbs
BR-8.description: Kerbstones along Brazilian roads are frequently painted white.

xx_pole_01.title: Ladder poles
xx_pole_01.description: The poles you often see in Brazil have a ladder-like design at the base. They have horizontal sections near the bottom.

NL-22.title: Brick Architecture
NL-22.description: Buildings are mostly red-brown brick with roofs of orange or dark grey tiles.

nl_general_01.title: Super flat
nl_general_01.description: The Netherlands is a very flat country. You won't find many hills here.

nl_license-plates_01.title: Yellow plates
nl_license-plates_01.description: In the Netherlands license plates are yellow, quite a rare sight in Europe.

xx_general_01_22.title: Brick roads
xx_general_01_22.description: Brick roads are common throughout the Netherlands.

a_general_01_06.title: Mountains all around
a_general_01_06.description: Andorra is located in a mountain range between France and Spain, this leads to mountains being visible at all times.

xx_general_01_35.title: Stone buildings
xx_general_01_35.description: Stone buildings are common all across Andorra.

US-48.title: Rocky Mountains
US-48.description: Jagged, rocky formations from the Canadian border to northern New Mexico, often with pine forests and snow on high peaks.

US-49-idaho.title: Idaho Great Basin
US-49-idaho.description: Greener dry plains with patches of grass and shrubs, and occasional low mountain ranges.

EC-13.title: Grey Brick Architecture
EC-13.description: Houses are mostly grey cinder blocks with corrugated metal roofs.

EC-18.title: Elevation and Terrain
EC-18.description: The Andes run through the center, with flat terrain on the Pacific coast and Amazon basin.

CL-13.title: Atacama and Coquimbo Mountains
CL-13.description: Jagged, uneven rock formations dominate Atacama and northern Coquimbo.

ZA-1.title: Yellow Edge Lines
ZA-1.description: Most South African roads feature single yellow edge lines paired with white centre lines.

ph_misc_01.title: City abbreviations
ph_misc_01.description: In the Philippines city abbreviations can often be found on boxes mounted on utility poles.

xx_language_01_04.title: English
xx_language_01_04.description: English is one of the official languages in the Philippines and appears on signs frequently.

AR-13.title: Grassland with Plantations
AR-13.description: Open grasslands dotted with scattered clusters of planted trees.

AR-14.title: Buenos Aires Lakes
AR-14.description: Roadside ponds and small bodies of water appear in Buenos Aires province.

BD-10.title: Tin Roofs
BD-10.description: Corrugated metal roofing is widespread on residential buildings.

xx_general_01_15.title: Bengali language
xx_general_01_15.description: Bengali is an official language of Bangladesh, and its script has a horizontal line across the top of each word.

VN-11.title: Holey Concrete Poles
VN-11.description: Concrete poles with rows of holes, on the lower half or nearly to the top, are common in Vietnam.

VN-14.title: Double Poles
VN-14.description: Double utility poles of various designs are fairly common in Vietnam.

VN-56.title: Hoi An Yellow Buildings
VN-56.description: Hoi An is identifiable by old yellow buildings with dark brown doors and details.

s_general_01_21.title: Alpine architecture
s_general_01_21.description: Slovenian buildings are alpine-inspired with light-colored walls and dark wooden details.

ID-20.title: Central Sulawesi Secondary Poles
ID-20.description: Slender black secondary poles beside main utility poles with two strips of tape near the top.

AU-3.title: White Road Lines
AU-3.description: Australian roads use white markings almost everywhere.

AU-72.title: Brisbane Street Signs
AU-72.description: Brisbane City Council street signs have a distinctive design.

AU-8.title: Speed Limit Signs
AU-8.description: Speed limits show a black number in a red ring on a white rectangular plate.

us_road-signs_01.title: Speed signs
us_road-signs_01.description: Speed signs in the US say ‘Speed Limit’.

GB-19.title: Chimney Pots
GB-19.description: Brick chimney stacks topped with multiple cylindrical terracotta pots.

GB-2.title: Double Yellow Road Lines
GB-2.description: Paired yellow lines along the kerbside mark no-stopping zones in towns and cities.

u_general_01_07.title: White and yellow
u_general_01_07.description: In the UK, license plates are yellow in the rear and white on the front.

c_general_01_06.title: Yellow or white lines
c_general_01_06.description: Chile can have either fully yellow or fully white lines. The two colors are almost never combined.

PE-13.title: Semi-Arid Mountain Landscape
PE-13.description: Much of Peru has dry mountain ranges and valleys with sparse vegetation.

PE-17.title: Political Party Logos
PE-17.description: Peruvian political party logos are often painted on walls and buildings.

PE-35.title: Rocky Outcrops in the Central Highlands
PE-35.description: Exposed rock faces are common on hillsides in central Peru from Lago Chinchaycocha south to Ayacucho.

PE-36.title: Jagged Mountain Peaks
PE-36.description: Tall, sharp rocky peaks are typical from Huaraz south to Cusco, away from the coast.

PE-38.title: Dark Red Soil
PE-38.description: Reddish-tinted earth appears notably around Cusco, Ayacucho, Cajamarca, and Tarapoto.

PE-4.title: Road Line Markings
PE-4.description: Peruvian outer road lines are always white. Highways have single or double yellow centre lines. Rural mountain roads often lack a centre line.

FR-44.title: Topography
FR-44.description: Highest peaks are in the southeast (Alps) and along the Spanish border (Pyrenees). North and Atlantic coast are flat to rolling; southern interior is hillier.

GR-18.title: Red Soil
GR-18.description: Exposed red-tinted earth is widespread in the landscape.

GR-24.title: Western Mountains
GR-24.description: Highest peaks and most high-altitude roads are in the western mainland.

PH-8.title: Colourful Sign Posts
PH-8.description: Posts supporting road signs are frequently painted red, orange, or yellow.

MY-26.title: Mountainous Sabah vs Flat Sarawak
MY-26.description: Sabah is mountainous with steep roads; Sarawak is generally flatter.

m_general_01_05.title: Malay plates
m_general_01_05.description: Malaysian plates are black with two white sections, easily visible even through blurring.

LK-15.title: Tuk-Tuks
LK-15.description: Sri Lankan tuk-tuks are bulky with a black roof, typically painted green, yellow, or red.

lk_language_01.title: Sinhala writing
lk_language_01.description: The written Sri Lankan language Sinhala have letters that are very round. Some letter makes it look like there are small doodle characters among us.

lk_road_01.title: Driving direction
lk_road_01.description: In Sri Lanka they drive on the left side of the road.

xx_license-plates_01_06.title: White and yellow
xx_license-plates_01_06.description: Sri Lankan license plates are white in the front and yellow in the rear.

SK-17.title: Slovak vs Czech Language Differences
SK-17.description: Slovak uses unique accented letters like L with caron (Ľ) and O with circumflex (Ô); Czech uses others like R with caron (Ř) and U with ring (Ů).

SK-32.title: Spring Coverage
SK-32.description: Most imagery was captured in spring.

SK-4.title: Inverted Triangle Pole Supports
SK-4.description: Two angled braces create upside-down triangle silhouette.

NZ-48.title: Tightly Spaced Wooden Fence Posts
NZ-48.description: Wooden fences with closely packed posts are prevalent on the North Island, northern South Island, and around Akaroa.

NZ-6.title: Blue Street Signs
NZ-6.description: New Zealand street signs are predominantly blue with white text, especially in rural areas.

NZ-7.title: Road Line Markings
NZ-7.description: NZ outer road lines are generally white; centre lines are single white dashes or solid double yellow lines.

xx_road_01_03.title: Intersection triangles
xx_road_01_03.description: Triangles can be found painted on the road at intersections in New Zealand.

NZ-1.title: Licence Plates
NZ-1.description: New Zealand plates are white with black lettering, appearing almost entirely white when blurred.

xx_general_01_28.title: Red text
xx_general_01_28.description: In New Zealand, Give Way signs feature red text and a small white outline.

xx_general_01_20.title: Green sticker
xx_general_01_20.description: In Germany, most cars have a green circular sticker on the bottom right of the windshield.

BR-41.title: Wooden Poles
BR-41.description: Timber utility poles prevalent in Rio Grande do Sul, Roraima, Amazonas, and Rio de Janeiro.

br_language_01.title: Portuguese
br_language_01.description: Brazil is the only South American country that uses the Portuguese language. It has the letter “Ç”, something Spanish does not.

NZ-2.title: Concrete Utility Poles with Single Groove
NZ-2.description: NZ's main poles are concrete with a single long vertical groove and small silver possum guards.

NZ-34.title: Square Concrete Poles without Groove
NZ-34.description: Square-profile concrete poles lacking vertical grooves are most common in Southland.

NZ-35.title: Off-Centre Crossbars on Poles
NZ-35.description: Utility poles with uneven, asymmetrical crossbars appear in Otago, Marlborough, Wellington, and Taranaki.

NZ-41.title: Long Black Vertical Sticker (6 Digits with Square)
NZ-41.description: Tall black vertical stickers with six digits and a small black square appear across much of the North Island and in Southland and Otago.

co_vehicles_01.title: Taxi
co_vehicles_01.description: Taxi cars will often feature useful information such as the name of the city they are driving in.

ES-11.title: Flat Signposts
ES-11.description: Nearly all traffic signs, kilometre markers, and chevrons are mounted on flat-profile signposts.

ES-15.title: Spanish Language
ES-15.description: Spanish is dominant; the letter Ñ is exclusive to Spanish.

ES-18.title: Landscape Diversity
ES-18.description: Spain's scenery ranges from lush forests and plateaus to semi-deserts and mountains.

ES-19.title: Mediterranean Climate
ES-19.description: Most of the country has a dry Mediterranean climate reflected in vegetation and agriculture.

xx_road-signs_01_01.title: Spanish chevrons
xx_road-signs_01_01.description: In Spain, you can find both black and white chevrons and blue and white chevrons.

ES-101.title: Canary Islands Landscapes
ES-101.description: Diverse landscapes: volcanic mountains, pine forests, lava fields, arid zones, and Mediterranean-like countryside.

ES-102.title: Lanzarote Volcanic Soil
ES-102.description: Very dark exposed volcanic terrain, almost lunar in places, is more abundant on Lanzarote than on any other Canary Island.

ES-105.title: Lanzarote Wine Plantations
ES-105.description: Unique vineyards where each vine is sheltered inside a semicircular stone wall built on dark volcanic soil.

ES-2.title: Ladder Poles and Wooden Poles
ES-2.description: Common poles include concrete 'ladder' poles with step-like indentations and plain wooden poles.

PE-0.title: Licence Plates
PE-0.description: Peruvian plates are white or yellow; taxis have split-coloured plates, yellow on top and white on bottom.

PE-15.title: Red-and-White Vehicle Stickers
PE-15.description: Wide red-and-white reflective stickers are common on taxis and commercial vehicles in Peru.

PE-24.title: Southwestern Piura, Dry Flat Terrain
PE-24.description: Southwest of Piura is dry, sparsely vegetated, mostly flat with gentle hills.

pe_vehicles_01.title: Tuk tuks
pe_vehicles_01.description: Tuk Tuks are a common sight in Peru. They are usually referred to as mototaxi.

ES-94.title: Balearic Islands Landscape
ES-94.description: Coastal Mediterranean feel with dry Aleppo pine forests on hillsides and small agricultural patches of fruit and olive trees.

ES-95.title: Balearic Rock Walls
ES-95.description: Low dry-stone walls are extremely prevalent throughout the Balearic Islands.

US-167.title: Missing Front Plates
US-167.description: About 22 states require only a rear plate; vehicles without front plates likely come from these states.

FI-12.title: Wooden Utility Poles
FI-12.description: Plain timber poles with various top fittings; street lights often mounted directly on them.

FI-15.title: Boreal Forests
FI-15.description: Thick coniferous forests dominated by pine and spruce, with birch trees having bright white bark.

FI-2.title: Middle Road Lines
FI-2.description: Centre lines appear as white dashes, solid white, solid yellow, or double yellow lines.

f_general_01_06.title: Snow poles
f_general_01_06.description: Finland has orange snow poles with a single narrow white band positioned close to the top.

fi_architecture_01.title: Red houses
fi_architecture_01.description: Along Sweden and Norway, Finland has many of these distinct red houses with white trim.

CH-3.title: Direction Signs
CH-3.description: Sign colour signals road class: blue for main roads, white for secondary roads.

xx_road-signs_01_02.title: Framed Signs
xx_road-signs_01_02.description: In Switzerland, many road signs have a thin metal border that gives them a clean, framed look.

MX-11.title: Rooftop Water Tanks
MX-11.description: Wide cylindrical water tanks, usually black or white, are common on Mexican rooftops.

MX-15.title: American Car Brands and Pickup Trucks
MX-15.description: US vehicle brands and pickup trucks are very popular on Mexican roads.

mx_pole_01.title: Octagonal poles
mx_pole_01.description: Mexico usually has octagonal utility poles made of concrete.

xx_general_01_17.title: Electricity meters
xx_general_01_17.description: Mexico, along with several Central American countries, uses circular electricity meters.

TH-27.title: Rice Cultivation Zone
TH-27.description: Most of Thailand's rice farming takes place within the highlighted region.

TH-5.title: Utility Poles
TH-5.description: Thai utility poles are square-profiled concrete with a vertical row of small pinholes up the shaft.

th_language_01.title: Small circles
th_language_01.description: In the written Thai language there is a lot of small circles on the letters.

PL-0.title: Licence Plates
PL-0.description: Polish plates are long and white with the standard EU blue strip on the left.

PL-12.title: Flat Green Landscape
PL-12.description: Poland features flat terrain with gentle hills, extensive agriculture, and moderate forest cover.

pl_general_01.title: Holy poles
pl_general_01.description: The utility poles in Poland are often thin and features a lot of holes. These holes usually don't go all the way down.

xx_road-signs_01_03.title: Warning signs
xx_road-signs_01_03.description: Poland's warning signs are triangular with a yellow background and a thin red border.

BR-20.title: Caatinga
BR-20.description: Northeast interior features dry soil, thorny scrub, and succulents of the Caatinga biome.

BR-30.title: Babassu Palms
BR-30.description: Large palms with heavy leaflet fronds found throughout the Amazon and eastern seaboard.

BR-35.title: Tall Roadside Grass
BR-35.description: Exceptionally tall grass flanking roads in Tocantins, Goiás, Bahia, and Minas Gerais.

ID-2.title: Road Markings
ID-2.description: Centre lines can be white or yellow; edge lines are always white.

ID-7.title: Red-and-White Banners
ID-7.description: Strings of small red and white pennants, the national colours, hung along roads throughout the archipelago.

MX-59.title: Hanging Insulators on Concrete Poles
MX-59.description: Concrete power poles with insulators hanging below the crossbar are typical of the Yucatan peninsula.

d_general_01_07.title: Flat landscape
d_general_01_07.description: The terrain across Denmark is predominantly flat.

NZ-12.title: State Highway Numbering System
NZ-12.description: New Zealand's two-digit state highway numbers run north to south sequentially.

NZ-5.title: White Sign Posts
NZ-5.description: NZ directional and warning signs are typically mounted on white posts; warning signs are yellow diamonds.

NZ-9.title: Green Directional Signs
NZ-9.description: New Zealand highway direction signs are green with state highway numbers inside a red shield.

v_general_01.title: Concrete bollards
v_general_01.description: Small concrete bollards are the most common ones in Vietnam. They have a red top.

xx_general_01_31.title: Vietnamese language
xx_general_01_31.description: The Vietnamese language is written in a modified Latin script that features an extensive system of diacritical marks.

SE-14.title: Striped Signpost Markings
SE-14.description: Swedish signposts often have coloured striped markings, commonly blue-and-white or red-and-yellow.

SE-15.title: Red-and-Yellow Road Infrastructure
SE-15.description: Road infrastructure and work signs in Sweden are often painted red and yellow.

SE-16.title: Street Name Suffixes
SE-16.description: Swedish street names often end in "vägen" or "gatan," abbreviated as "v" and "g" on signs.

SE-44.title: Birch Rows Along the North Coast
SE-44.description: Long rows of thin birch trees line urban streets in northern coastal towns.

FI-17.title: Lakes
FI-17.description: Finland has many lakes appearing frequently across the landscape.

FI-5.title: Finnish Language
FI-5.description: Finnish has long words, frequent double vowels, and special characters ä and ö.

f_general_01.title: Shorter plates
f_general_01.description: In Finland, license plates are slightly shorter than in most other European countries, and they include the standard EU blue strip on the left.

f_general_01_08.title: Crossing signs
f_general_01_08.description: Finnish pedestrian crossing signs feature five black stripes.

GR-1.title: Greek Alphabet
GR-1.description: Greek is written in its distinctive script with rounder, softer lowercase forms.

GR-16.title: Mediterranean Architecture
GR-16.description: Stone buildings with white or pastel walls and orange tile roofs; islands feature white walls with blue doors and windows.

g_general_01_10.title: Greek plates
g_general_01_10.description: Greek license plates are either fully white or follow the standard EU layout with a blue strip on the left side.

g_general_01_11.title: Wooden poles
g_general_01_11.description: Most Greek utility poles are made of timber, often seen in a dark brown tone.

RU-13.title: Soviet-Era Apartment Blocks
RU-13.description: Russian urban housing mostly consists of large rectangular concrete blocks with plain facades.

RU-2.title: Word for Street
RU-2.description: Russian word for street is улица (ulitsa), shortened to ул.

RU-flag.title: Country Flag
RU-flag.description: The national flag of Russia is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

xx_general_01_55.title: Long, white plates
xx_general_01_55.description: Russian plates are entirely white with black text and lack the blue EU-style strip found on most European plates.

US-117.title: Red Metal Rooftops
US-117.description: Red metal roofs are a common sight in the southeastern U.S.

US-43.title: Appalachian Mountains
US-43.description: A low mountain range in the eastern US, covered in forest with beech and oak trees.

CA-58.title: PEI Red Soil
CA-58.description: Prince Edward Island is known for its red-tinted earth and potato farming.

c_general_01_09.title: French to the east
c_general_01_09.description: In Canada, written French will mainly be found in the provinces of Québec and New Brunswick.

ES-42.title: Castilla y León Flatlands
ES-42.description: Broad, gently undulating agricultural plain dominated by cereal crops and occasional sunflower fields.

KE-21.title: Kitui (Semi-Arid)
KE-21.description: Kitui area is semi-arid, hilly or mountainous, with light orange sandy soil.

s_general_01_24.title: Snow poles
s_general_01_24.description: Swedish snow poles are typically orange with a tall white reflector positioned slightly above the midpoint.

BO-14.title: Tigo Telecom Branding
BO-14.description: Tigo's blue logo appears frequently in Bolivian urban areas.

BO-3.title: Road Line Colours
BO-3.description: Centre road markings vary between solid yellow, mixed yellow and white, or solid white; edge lines are always white.

br_misc_01.title: Phone numbers
br_misc_01.description: Phone numbers in Brazil often include an area code as a separate two-digit prefix.

PH-12.title: Grain Drying on Roads
PH-12.description: Harvested grain is often spread out on roads for drying.

PH-29.title: Chile-Style Indented Concrete Poles
PH-29.description: Square concrete utility poles with a visible indent on each side are found mainly north of Manila and around Bacolod on Negros.

PH-25.title: Amakan Walls with Diamond Pattern
PH-25.description: Houses with woven bamboo walls in a diamond pattern are found almost exclusively in the southern half of the Philippines.

BR-37.title: Sugarcane
BR-37.description: Sugarcane fields concentrated in São Paulo and the northeastern coast, especially Alagoas and Pernambuco.

BR-40.title: Round Concrete Poles
BR-40.description: Cylindrical concrete poles common in southern states and São Paulo; large cities use round poles.

AU-16.title: Trident Pole Tops
AU-16.description: Pole tops shaped like a three-pronged fork appear in Western Australia and Victoria.

TR-21.title: Interlocking Brick Pavements
TR-21.description: Sidewalks and pedestrian areas often use interlocking bricks in a repeating shape.

TR-38.title: Metal Roofs in the East
TR-38.description: Sheet metal roofing is common in eastern Turkey.

US-75.title: Thick Yellow Centre Lines, WV, VA, MD
US-75.description: Some roads in West Virginia, Virginia, and Maryland have centre yellow lines that are noticeably thicker than standard.

US-24.title: Long-Nose Semi-Trucks
US-24.description: North American semi-trucks have a long nose with the engine ahead of the cab.

US-49-utah.title: Utah Great Basin
US-49-utah.description: Dry, open plains with scattered sagebrush and distant high mountain ranges in western and central Utah.

ES-63.title: Baltic Pines
ES-63.description: Pinus sylvestris grows tall and slender with dark bark that sheds near the top to reveal orange-red wood. The lower trunk is usually branchless. Found mainly in the Pyrenees, Sierra de Guadarrama, and the Iberian System.

ES-64.title: Maritime Pines (Atlantic)
ES-64.description: Near the Atlantic coast, Pinus pinaster shows grey bark with red undertones and fluffy upward-pointing branches. Mature trees lose their lower branches.

ES-65.title: Maritime Pines (Mediterranean)
ES-65.description: Away from the Atlantic, Pinus pinaster has grey, deeply fissured bark with red tones. Found in mountain ranges across central and southern Spain.

BG-0.title: Licence Plates
BG-0.description: Bulgarian plates have a blue EU band on the left side.

BG-16.title: Orange Roof Tiles
BG-16.description: Houses have orange clay tile roofs with visible mortar patches and uneven tilework.

BG-6.title: Concrete Utility Poles
BG-6.description: Dominant poles are round concrete cylinders.

b_general_01_14.title: Metal waste bins
b_general_01_14.description: It is common to spot these metal waste bins in Bulgaria.

PE-30.title: Flat Highland Plateaus
PE-30.description: Flat high-altitude terrain appears in central Puno and around Lake Chinchaycocha.

BD-16.title: Mid-Growth Rice
BD-16.description: Medium-height green rice indicates mid-season growth in Rangpur, Barishal, and Chittagong.

BD-8.title: White-Painted Tree Trunks
BD-8.description: Roads are often lined with trees whose lower trunks are painted white.

DK-0.title: Licence Plates
DK-0.description: Danish plates: standard white with blue EU band, yellow for commercial vehicles, and unique 'Parrot' variant with yellow left section.

DK-16.title: Red-and-White Chevrons
DK-16.description: Curve warning boards in Denmark are red and white and tend to be positioned close to the ground.

DK-18.title: Roadside Bicycle Paths
DK-18.description: Dedicated cycle lanes running alongside the carriageway are a frequent feature of Danish roads.

DK-7.title: Danish Language
DK-7.description: Danish is a North Germanic language with letters Æ, Ø, and Å.

DK-flag.title: Country Flag
DK-flag.description: The national flag of Denmark is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

AE-5.title: Arabic and English
AE-5.description: Signage in the UAE is bilingual, with Arabic script alongside English.

AE-flag.title: UAE flag
AE-flag.description: Horizontal stripes of green, white, and black with a vertical red band on the left.

a_general_01_01.title: Unpaved roads
a_general_01_01.description: Despite the country's wealth, it is not unusual to encounter unpaved roads in residential areas.

IE-12.title: Green Hedgerow Landscape
IE-12.description: Lush farmland bordered by dense hedgerows dominates the country.

IE-2.title: Architecture
IE-2.description: Rural houses are cream with dark slate roofs; urban streets have terraced row houses.

IE-9.title: Rounded-Corner Farm Gates
IE-9.description: Metal field gates almost always have rounded top corners.

i_general_01.title: Dashed outer lines
i_general_01.description: Irish roads often have dashed yellow outlines.

m_general_01_06.title: Red block
m_general_01_06.description: North Macedonian plates are white and can have the blue EU strip. A noticeable red block sits near the left side.

ES-39.title: Green Northern Coast
ES-39.description: The far north is lush with rolling hills, hedgerows, and verdant meadows.

ES-41.title: Pyrenean Pine Forests
ES-41.description: Dense tall pine forests cover much of the Pyrenees and smaller hills in the Basque Country or Navarre.

VN-5.title: Waystones with Coloured Tops
VN-5.description: Vietnamese waystones are white with red or blue tops, showing road numbers and distances.

KE-6.title: Red-and-White Road Signs
KE-6.description: Road signs in Kenya are mostly red and white.

BD-0.title: Licence Plates
BD-0.description: Vehicles in Bangladesh have licence plates in white, black, or turquoise.

b_general_01_03.title: Triangular letters
b_general_01_03.description: Bengali, the language in Bangladesh has got a lot of triangular shapes, something similar scripts do not feature.

xx_pole_01_05.title: Concrete poles
xx_pole_01_05.description: You will find rectangular, indented concrete poles in Chile. The upper part typically has small pinholes.

SE-1.title: Swedish Language
SE-1.description: Swedish is a North Germanic language with the letters Å, Ä, and Ö.

SE-25.title: Broad-Leafed Trees
SE-25.description: Broad-leafed trees grow naturally only in southern Sweden and increase further south.

CA-38.title: 'Arrêt' Stop Signs
CA-38.description: Stop signs displaying only the French word 'Arrêt' are found exclusively in Québec.

CA-96.title: Quebec Licence Plate
CA-96.description: Québec plates appear white with a dark bluish tint.

DE-35.title: Dark Reflector Bollards
DE-35.description: Bollards with noticeably darker reflectors appear in certain regions.

z_general_01.title: Green directional signs
z_general_01.description: South African directional signs are green with yellow road numbers. Road-numbers starting with N or R are exclusive to South Africa.

GB-9.title: White Street Signs
GB-9.description: Low-mounted white plaques with black lettering, often on two short posts; suburban versions may show cul-de-sac pictograms.

u_general_01_09.title: Terraced houses
u_general_01_09.description: Two-story, terraced buildings are extremely common in the UK.

EC-0.title: Licence Plates
EC-0.description: Private plates in Ecuador are white in short and long formats. Taxis and buses use orange plates.

xx_general_01_08.title: Ecuadorian bollards
xx_general_01_08.description: In Ecuador, bollards are typically either thin and round with two red stripes or flat with two red reflectors.

BR-77.title: Irregular Cobblestone Roads
BR-77.description: Streets paved with uneven stones are common in southeastern Rio Grande do Sul and Minas Gerais.

BR-78.title: Rough Square-Stone Roads
BR-78.description: Bumpy roads of roughly square-cut stones appear in western Rio Grande do Sul and Santa Catarina.

xx_misc_01_07.title: Electricity boxes
xx_misc_01_07.description: Grey electricity boxes can be seen mounted to utility poles in Vietnam. They are tapered towards the bottom and have a few windows.

e_general_01_05.title: Estonian bollard
e_general_01_05.description: Estonian bollards have a rounded profile. The front carries a rectangular reflector while the back has two circular ones, in either white or orange.

MX-23.title: Pulque Agaves
MX-23.description: Agave salmiana has broad, smooth, curling leaves forming a crown-like silhouette, thriving in the central valley and around San Luis Potosi.

MX-67.title: Irregular Cobblestone Pavement
MX-67.description: Streets paved with randomly arranged, irregular cobblestones are widespread in central Mexico, especially Nayarit, Jalisco, Colima, and Queretaro.

CA-27.title: Québec Pole Labels
CA-27.description: Québec utility poles sometimes display a vertical sticker split black and yellow, with a small 'Q' in the black half.

e_general_01_07.title: Many stripes
e_general_01_07.description: On the Spanish crossing signs there are eight stripes, the most in all of Europe.

TW-11.title: Architecture
TW-11.description: Taiwanese residential buildings range from cramped multi-storey to flat single-storey homes, often boxy with white tile walls and light-green tin sheds.

TW-20.title: Central-Eastern Mountains
TW-20.description: Forested mountains cover two-thirds of Taiwan with temperate or coniferous trees at higher elevations.

TW-3.title: Double Yellow Centre Lines
TW-3.description: Most Taiwanese roads have double yellow centre lines with single white edge lines.

TW-9.title: Concrete Drainage Ditches
TW-9.description: Open concrete drainage channels run alongside many Taiwanese roads.

t_general_01_03.title: Traditional Chinese
t_general_01_03.description: Taiwanese signage uses Traditional Chinese, a complex script with intricate multi-stroke characters.

t_general_01_04.title: Pole markings
t_general_01_04.description: In Taiwan, nearly all utility poles carry diagonal black-and-yellow striped markings that most often run all the way down to the ground.

MX-10.title: Yellow-Painted Kerbs and Barriers
MX-10.description: Kerbs and bridge barriers are frequently painted yellow in Mexico.

DE-13.title: No-Stopping Arrow Signs
DE-13.description: No Stopping and No Waiting signs often include white directional arrows on the sign face.

TH-10.title: Directional Road Signs
TH-10.description: Minor-road directional signs are white with two stacked panels; highways have green signs often with romanised names.

TH-4.title: Concrete Roads
TH-4.description: Paved concrete surfaces in Thailand typically display a large square-tile pattern.

TH-7.title: Yellow Centre Lines
TH-7.description: Thai road centre markings are yellow, either solid or dashed lines.

TH-9.title: Overhanging Lamp Posts
TH-9.description: Thai lamp posts are long and slender, arcing outward over the roadway.

th_road_01.title: Driving direction
th_road_01.description: In Thailand they drive on the left side of the road.

VN-9.title: Concrete Block Roads
VN-9.description: Minor Vietnamese roads are often made of concrete blocks.

NZ-11.title: Ferns in Forested Areas
NZ-11.description: Ferns are very common in New Zealand's wooded and forested areas.

NZ-17.title: Waikato and Northland Landscape
NZ-17.description: These regions feature dry conditions and rolling hills; Northland is notably hilly.

NZ-27.title: Very Tall Hedges in Bay of Plenty
NZ-27.description: Exceptionally tall hedges are characteristic around Tauranga in the Bay of Plenty.

NZ-65.title: Fruit Farms with Green Netting
NZ-65.description: Orchards draped in green protective netting are especially common around Tauranga and occasionally near Gisborne.

RU-43.title: Caspian Steppe
RU-43.description: The area west of the Caspian Sea is extremely dry and flat, especially in Kalmykia, Astrakhan, and Dagestan.

RU-62.title: White Limestone Brick Buildings
RU-62.description: White limestone brick buildings indicate Dagestan and nearby areas.

RU-96.title: Rural Desert Coverage
RU-96.description: Flat rural desert-like roads west of the Caspian Sea appear only in northern Dagestan and southwestern Astrakhan.

xx_general_01_41.title: Black socks
xx_general_01_41.description: In Russia, signposts often have their lower sections painted black.

RU-29.title: Sandy Roadsides
RU-29.description: Sandy roadsides are typical in Khanty-Mansi, Yamalo-Nenets, near Nizhny Novgorod, Karelia, Murmansk, and western Sakha.

TH-12.title: Garuda Road Markers
TH-12.description: Thai route-number markers feature a white or black Garuda symbol; national routes are white-and-black shields, provincial routes blue-and-yellow.

SE-10.title: Directional Signs
SE-10.description: Most Swedish directional signs are blue with white text and an arrow, while yellow signs with black text are typically used for smaller local destinations.

SE-33.title: Lake Mälaren Landscape
SE-33.description: Around Lake Mälaren, flat terrain has medium fields, forests in the background, and small tree clusters in fields.

SE-69.title: Place Name Endings
SE-69.description: Certain place name suffixes are region-specific, useful for pinpointing locations.

se_architecture_01.title: Red houses
se_architecture_01.description: In the countryside Sweden, along with Norway and Finland, has many of these distinct red houses with white trim.

ph_road_01_01.title: Driving direction
ph_road_01_01.description: They drive on the right side of the road in the Philippines.

SE-51.title: Light-Coloured Houses on the West Coast
SE-51.description: The west coast has many white and light yellow houses, especially between Gothenburg and Norway.

VN-4.title: Yellow-Orange Road Signs
VN-4.description: Vietnamese road signs have a yellow-orange background.

VN-8.title: Short Yellow Centre Dashes
VN-8.description: Short yellow dashes as centre road lines are common and distinctive in Vietnam.

RU-42.title: Omsk Oblast Landscape
RU-42.description: Omsk Oblast shows green agricultural fields broken by isolated birch forest patches in summer.

MX-38.title: Golden Roadside Grass Tufts
MX-38.description: Lines of golden grass tufts growing immediately beside roads in Coahuila.

FR-31.title: Telephone Area Codes
FR-31.description: Phone numbers are ten digits; first pairs indicate broad zones, with 06–09 for mobile and non-regional.

CA-12.title: Provincial Speed Sign Variants
CA-12.description: Ontario speed signs may include a black strip reading 'km/h' or 'begins'. British Columbia shows 'km/h' without the black section. Québec signs sometimes include French text.

CA-17.title: Québec Fire Hydrant Markers
CA-17.description: Yellow markers on top of signposts indicate underground fire hydrants throughout Québec.

CA-61.title: Quebec Provincial Flags
CA-61.description: Provincial flag, Québec's Fleurdelisé, is commonly displayed on buildings and roads.

NO-43.title: Coastal Grasslands
NO-43.description: Roads along the far northern coast pass through open grasslands with minimal vegetation and low, distant mountains.

no_nature_01.title: Beautiful views
no_nature_01.description: Fjords are a common sight along the Norwegian coast.

US-8.title: Green Highway Exit Signs
US-8.description: Large green signs with white text mark exits and distances on US highways.

NL-1.title: Dutch Language
NL-1.description: Dutch is a Germanic language with frequent double vowels and distinctive letter combinations like 'ij'.

NL-21.title: Striped Road Barriers
NL-21.description: Red-and-white striped barriers are common along Dutch roads, especially rural areas.

NL-8.title: All-White Road Markings
NL-8.description: Dutch road lines are entirely white, with common dashed edge lines and occasional green centre lines.

xx_language_01.title: Afrikaans
xx_language_01.description: South Africa has eleven official languages. While English dominates signage, the Dutch-like language Afrikaans has had a big influence on for example city names.

SN.title: Bakel, Dry Hills
SN.description: Dry terrain with gentle hills appears around Bakel and south to Nayé.

SN.title: French colonial influence
SN.description: In Senegal, French is the official language and dominates all visible signage.

CA.title: Centre Line Markings
CA.description: Canadian roads commonly use a single yellow centre line; double yellow lines also appear.

CA.title: Sun visible to the south
CA.description: The sun appears toward the south, which usually points to a northern-hemisphere location.

CA.title: Vehicles drive on the right
CA.description: Traffic here appears to drive on the right side of the road.

CA.title: Transformer Orientation (BC & NB)
CA.description: Pole-mounted transformers in British Columbia and New Brunswick face the road; elsewhere they align with the wires.

CA.title: Western Mountains
CA.description: Major mountain ranges are concentrated in British Columbia, western Alberta, and parts of Yukon.

CA.title: Québec City–Windsor Corridor
CA.description: Canada's most populated zone, a flat green belt mixing farmland and woodland between Québec City and Windsor.

CA.title: Area Codes
CA.description: Canadian phone numbers start with a three-digit area code in the format XXX XXX XXXX.

CA.title: Speed signs
CA.description: Speed signs in Canada say ‘Maximum’. This word works in both English and French, the official languages of Canada.

CA.title: Checkered signs
CA.description: In Canada, T-intersection signs are diamond-shaped and have a distinctive checkered pattern.

CA.title: BC Concrete Barriers
CA.description: British Columbia favours solid concrete barriers over metal guardrails on highways.

CA.title: PEI Red Soil
CA.description: Prince Edward Island is known for its red-tinted earth and potato farming.

CA.title: French to the east
CA.description: In Canada, written French will mainly be found in the provinces of Québec and New Brunswick.

CA.title: 'Arrêt' Stop Signs
CA.description: Stop signs displaying only the French word 'Arrêt' are found exclusively in Québec.

CA.title: Quebec Licence Plate
CA.description: Québec plates appear white with a dark bluish tint.

CA.title: Québec Pole Labels
CA.description: Québec utility poles sometimes display a vertical sticker split black and yellow, with a small 'Q' in the black half.

CA.title: Provincial Speed Sign Variants
CA.description: Ontario speed signs may include a black strip reading 'km/h' or 'begins'. British Columbia shows 'km/h' without the black section. Québec signs sometimes include French text.

CA.title: Québec Fire Hydrant Markers
CA.description: Yellow markers on top of signposts indicate underground fire hydrants throughout Québec.

CA.title: Quebec Provincial Flags
CA.description: Provincial flag, Québec's Fleurdelisé, is commonly displayed on buildings and roads.

GB.title: Wooden Poles with Steps
GB.description: Timber utility poles have thin horizontal metal rungs bolted up one side.

GB.title: Chimney Pots
GB.description: Brick chimney stacks topped with multiple cylindrical terracotta pots.

GB.title: Double Yellow Road Lines
GB.description: Paired yellow lines along the kerbside mark no-stopping zones in towns and cities.

GB.title: White and yellow
GB.description: In the UK, license plates are yellow in the rear and white on the front.

GB.title: White Street Signs
GB.description: Low-mounted white plaques with black lettering, often on two short posts; suburban versions may show cul-de-sac pictograms.

GB.title: Terraced houses
GB.description: Two-story, terraced buildings are extremely common in the UK.

OM.title: Wooden Utility Poles
OM.description: Wooden power poles in Oman have three distinct top designs, including a unique metal triangle above one variant.

OM.title: Arabic
OM.description: Arabic is Oman's sole official language; signage often appears in Arabic and English.

OM.title: Yellow Edge Lines with White Centre Lines
OM.description: Omani roads have yellow lines along edges and white lines down the centre.

OM.title: Black-and-Yellow Curbs
OM.description: Kerbs painted in alternating black and yellow segments are widespread on Omani roads.

OM.title: Light Stone Architecture with Ornate Fences
OM.description: Omani homes are pale stone with decorative details, enclosed by matching stone fences with elaborate gates.

OM.title: Desert landscape
OM.description: Oman is dominated by arid, sparsely vegetated terrain. The central and southern interior is largely flat, while the northern coastline has dry, rugged mountains

ID.title: Satellite Dish Direction
ID.description: Satellite dishes aim towards the equator; dish direction indicates relative position to it.

ID.title: Utility Poles
ID.description: Cylindrical steel or concrete poles, some painted black with red-and-white bands. Crossbars may be symmetrical or asymmetrical.

ID.title: Clay Tile Roofs on Java
ID.description: Terracotta roof tiles are mainly a Javanese feature.

ID.title: Regional Licence Plate Codes
ID.description: Plate prefixes indicate region: single letters on western Java, two letters on eastern Java and other islands.

ID.title: Sun visible overhead
ID.description: The sun appears high overhead, which usually points to a location near the tropics.

ID.title: Corrugated Metal Roofs
ID.description: Sheet-metal roofing predominates in northern and outer islands like Kalimantan, Sulawesi, and Sumatra.

ID.title: Front Licence Plates on Motorcycles
ID.description: Indonesian motorcycles carry a front licence plate, unlike other Southeast Asian countries.

ID.title: Painted Fences on Sulawesi
ID.description: Roadside fences painted white with blue or red highlights are common on Sulawesi.

ID.title: Central Sulawesi Secondary Poles
ID.description: Slender black secondary poles beside main utility poles with two strips of tape near the top.

ID.title: Road Markings
ID.description: Centre lines can be white or yellow; edge lines are always white.

ID.title: Red-and-White Banners
ID.description: Strings of small red and white pennants, the national colours, hung along roads throughout the archipelago.

BR.title: Rio Grande do Sul
BR.description: Landscape alternates between rolling hills and flat green pastures.

BR.title: Paraná Pines
BR.description: Araucaria trees have long horizontal branches with foliage clustered at tips, found in Paraná, Santa Catarina, and Rio Grande do Sul.

BR.title: European-Influenced Architecture
BR.description: Southern states, especially Santa Catarina, feature buildings with Germanic architectural style.

BR.title: Orange Roof Tiles
BR.description: Terracotta-orange clay tiles are standard roofing material nationwide.

BR.title: Sun visible to the north
BR.description: The sun appears toward the north, which usually points to a southern-hemisphere location.

BR.title: Road Markings
BR.description: Centre lines are typically double solid yellow; edge lines are white.

BR.title: Transparent Satellite Dishes
BR.description: Clear or translucent satellite dishes on rooftops are common and unique in Latin America.

BR.title: Southeastern Rolling Hills
BR.description: Minas Gerais, Rio de Janeiro, and Espírito Santo have gentle grass-covered rolling hills.

BR.title: Exposed Rock Mountains
BR.description: Tall mountains with bare rock faces are common in Espírito Santo and nearby regions.

BR.title: Red soil
BR.description: This iron rich, red soil is primarily found in Brazil.

BR.title: Licence Plates
BR.description: Pre-2018 plates were plain white; current plates have a blue strip on top; commercial plates are red.

BR.title: Black signs
BR.description: Most road signs in Brazil have black backsides.

BR.title: Macaw Palms
BR.description: Narrow-leaved palms with pointed spear-shaped crowns, common around Mato Grosso do Sul.

BR.title: White-Painted Kerbs
BR.description: Kerbstones along Brazilian roads are frequently painted white.

BR.title: Ladder poles
BR.description: The poles you often see in Brazil have a ladder-like design at the base. They have horizontal sections near the bottom.

BR.title: Wooden Poles
BR.description: Timber utility poles prevalent in Rio Grande do Sul, Roraima, Amazonas, and Rio de Janeiro.

BR.title: Portuguese
BR.description: Brazil is the only South American country that uses the Portuguese language. It has the letter “Ç”, something Spanish does not.

BR.title: Caatinga
BR.description: Northeast interior features dry soil, thorny scrub, and succulents of the Caatinga biome.

BR.title: Babassu Palms
BR.description: Large palms with heavy leaflet fronds found throughout the Amazon and eastern seaboard.

BR.title: Tall Roadside Grass
BR.description: Exceptionally tall grass flanking roads in Tocantins, Goiás, Bahia, and Minas Gerais.

BR.title: Phone numbers
BR.description: Phone numbers in Brazil often include an area code as a separate two-digit prefix.

BR.title: Sugarcane
BR.description: Sugarcane fields concentrated in São Paulo and the northeastern coast, especially Alagoas and Pernambuco.

BR.title: Round Concrete Poles
BR.description: Cylindrical concrete poles common in southern states and São Paulo; large cities use round poles.

BR.title: Irregular Cobblestone Roads
BR.description: Streets paved with uneven stones are common in southeastern Rio Grande do Sul and Minas Gerais.

BR.title: Rough Square-Stone Roads
BR.description: Bumpy roads of roughly square-cut stones appear in western Rio Grande do Sul and Santa Catarina.

AU.title: Gum Trees (Eucalyptus)
AU.description: Eucalyptus trees have pale bark and rounded clumps of foliage.

AU.title: Upward-Angled Coil Pole Tops
AU.description: Queensland electricity poles often have side-mounted coils that tilt upwards.

AU.title: Short Bollard Reflectors
AU.description: Bollards with reflectors shorter than standard are concentrated in Queensland and South Australia.

AU.title: Tropical North Queensland
AU.description: Far north Queensland's coastal strip is lushly tropical with palms and dense dark green foliage.

AU.title: Sugarcane Fields
AU.description: Sugarcane fields dominate northern Queensland's tropical agricultural landscape.

AU.title: Chevrons
AU.description: Curve warning chevrons appear as white arrows on black or black arrows on yellow.

AU.title: Bollards
AU.description: Australian bollards are white with a vertical red stripe towards the top.

AU.title: Vehicles drive on the left
AU.description: Traffic here appears to drive on the left side of the road.

AU.title: White Road Lines
AU.description: Australian roads use white markings almost everywhere.

AU.title: Brisbane Street Signs
AU.description: Brisbane City Council street signs have a distinctive design.

AU.title: Speed Limit Signs
AU.description: Speed limits show a black number in a red ring on a white rectangular plate.

AU.title: Trident Pole Tops
AU.description: Pole tops shaped like a three-pronged fork appear in Western Australia and Victoria.

JP.title: White Guardrails
JP.description: Plain white guardrails are the default road barrier throughout Japan.

JP.title: Retaining Walls
JP.description: Retaining walls in remote countryside indicate you are in Japan.

JP.title: Japanese Writing Systems
JP.description: Japanese uses kanji, hiragana with rounded strokes, and angular katakana scripts.

JP.title: Architecture
JP.description: Building styles range from traditional rural houses to ultramodern urban high-rises.

JP.title: Round Concrete Poles
JP.description: Utility poles are round concrete with threaded screw-like protrusions and often electrical plates.

JP.title: Driving direction
JP.description: In Japan they drive on the left side of the road.

JP.title: Boxy cars
JP.description: In Japan small, boxy cars are very common. They are called Kei cars.

JP.title: Road Lines
JP.description: Japanese road markings include solid white edges with dashed or solid white/yellow center lines.

JP.title: Regional Pole Reflector Pads
JP.description: Reflector pads on utility poles vary in design by region.

JP.title: Cabbage
JP.description: Cabbage grows prolifically in Hokkaido and parts of northern Honshu, often visible beside roads.

JP.title: Hokkaido Winter Coverage
JP.description: Snowy winter Google Street View is scarce in Hokkaido, mostly in the southern part.

JP.title: Overhead arrows
JP.description: This arrow above the road marks the road during heavy snow and is mainly seen in Hokkaido.

JP.title: Pole markings
JP.description: Japanese poles often have thin, vertical yellow lines on a black section towards the bottom.

JP.title: Japanese White Birch
JP.description: This tree species is concentrated in Chubu and Hokkaido, with some presence in Tohoku.

RU.title: Summer Coverage
RU.description: Summer coverage is the most common and widespread.

RU.title: Cyrillic script
RU.description: Russian uses the Cyrillic alphabet. It is the only script showing up on most signs.

RU.title: Black-and-White Pole Shields
RU.description: Pole shields with alternating black and white stripes appear frequently along highways in European Russia.

RU.title: Bollard Types
RU.description: Russia has three main bollard styles: thin on a stick, black top with red reflector, and German-style.

RU.description: Mosques are most common in Muslim-majority areas: the North Caucasus republics, Tatarstan, and Bashkortostan.

RU.title: Country Flag
RU.description: The national flag of Russia is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

RU.title: Long, white plates
RU.description: Russian plates are entirely white with black text and lack the blue EU-style strip found on most European plates.

RU.title: Caspian Steppe
RU.description: The area west of the Caspian Sea is extremely dry and flat, especially in Kalmykia, Astrakhan, and Dagestan.

RU.title: White Limestone Brick Buildings

RU.description: Flat rural desert-like roads west of the Caspian Sea appear only in northern Dagestan and southwestern Astrakhan.

RU.description: In Russia, signposts often have their lower sections painted black.

RU.title: Sandy Roadsides
RU.description: Sandy roadsides are typical in Khanty-Mansi, Yamalo-Nenets, near Nizhny Novgorod, Karelia, Murmansk, and western Sakha.

RU.title: Omsk Oblast Landscape
RU.description: Omsk Oblast shows green agricultural fields broken by isolated birch forest patches in summer.

KE.title: Regional Climates
KE.description: Kenya spans humid to very arid climate zones; use climate as a regional clue.

KE.title: Grey Pickup Truck
KE.description: In a lot of the Kenyan coverage, you can see the large grey Street View pickup truck, sometimes with a black snorkel.

KE.title: County Names on Signage
KE.description: Signs often display Kenyan county names, useful for regional identification.

KE.title: Mobile network
KE.description: The mobile network Safaricom is exclusive to Kenya, and its branded signage appears in almost every town.

KE.title: Kitui (Semi-Arid)
KE.description: Kitui area is semi-arid, hilly or mountainous, with light orange sandy soil.

KE.title: Red-and-White Road Signs
KE.description: Road signs in Kenya are mostly red and white.

EC.description: Road bends have a high density of chevron signs.

EC.title: Grey Brick Architecture
EC.description: Houses are mostly grey cinder blocks with corrugated metal roofs.

EC.title: Elevation and Terrain
EC.description: The Andes run through the center, with flat terrain on the Pacific coast and Amazon basin.

EC.title: Licence Plates
EC.description: Private plates in Ecuador are white in short and long formats. Taxis and buses use orange plates.

EC.title: Ecuadorian bollards
EC.description: In Ecuador, bollards are typically either thin and round with two red stripes or flat with two red reflectors.

MY.title: Country Flag
MY.description: The national flag of Malaysia is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

MY.title: Mountainous Sabah vs Flat Sarawak
MY.description: Sabah is mountainous with steep roads; Sarawak is generally flatter.

MY.title: Malay plates
MY.description: Malaysian plates are black with two white sections, easily visible even through blurring.

DE.title: German Language
DE.description: Signs are in German, identifiable by Ä, Ö, Ü, and ß characters.

DE.title: Northwestern Brick Houses
