DE.title: Dark Sign Backs
DE.description: Road sign backs are often black or dark grey, with a small inverted red triangle sticker on most signs.

DE.title: Yellow 'H' Bus Stops
DE.description: Bus stops feature a yellow-and-green 'H' symbol.

DE.title: German bollard
DE.description: German bollards are black-and-white posts fitted with white or pale grey reflectors, switching to orange at intersections.

DE.description: Common German pole tops include horizontal crossarms with staggered insulators, inverted-triangle supports, and T-shaped arrangements.

DE.title: Green sticker
DE.description: In Germany, most cars have a green circular sticker on the bottom right of the windshield.

DE.title: Dark Reflector Bollards
DE.description: Bollards with noticeably darker reflectors appear in certain regions.

DE.title: No-Stopping Arrow Signs

AR.title: Road Lines

AR.title: Western Mountains

AR.title: Tierra del Fuego Grass
AR.description: Low, windswept grass with few shrubs signals Tierra del Fuego or SE Santa Cruz.

AR.title: Wooden Utility Poles
AR.description: Timber poles appear frequently, including unique A-frame variants.

AR.title: Wide Open Landscape

AR.description: Open grasslands dotted with scattered clusters of planted trees.

AR.title: Buenos Aires Lakes

US.title: Douglas Firs in Cascadia
US.description: Extremely tall conifers with dark brown bark and dark green foliage, common in Washington and Oregon.

US.title: Brown National Park Infrastructure
US.description: Guardrails, signs, and sign posts painted medium brown are characteristic of US national parks. Rock walls sometimes replace guardrails.

US.title: Wooden Utility Poles
US.description: North America predominantly uses wooden utility poles.

US.title: Water Towers
US.description: Tall water towers are common in US and Canadian towns, often displaying town or state names.

US.title: Sagebrush
US.description: Great Basin sagebrush is a short, shrubby blue-green bush common in arid interior western US.

US.title: Mailboxes
US.description: Mailboxes with a small flag are a common sight in North America.

US.title: Sheetz
US.description: Sheetz is a gas station and convenience store chain in the Eastern US, concentrated in the Mid-Atlantic and Central Appalachia.

US.title: Overhead Traffic Light Bars
US.description: Long metal arms with traffic lights, street signs, and highway signs extend over intersections throughout the US and Canada.

US.title: Road lines
US.description: US roads have yellow center lines (usually double) and white outer lines.

US.title: Yield signs
US.description: US yield signs are triangles with a red border and the word “YIELD” on a white background.

US.title: Thin Metal Sign Posts
US.description: Thin metal sign posts, either perforated or U-shaped, are standard in North America.

US.title: Nevada Great Basin
US.description: Vast, arid plains with low shrubs and isolated mountain ranges, often snow-capped in winter and spring.

US.title: Southwest Mesas and Red Rock
US.description: The Four Corners region features mesas, tablelands, and reddish rock formations with red soil.

US.title: Palm Trees
US.description: Common along the Southeast coast, Gulf Coast, and Desert Southwest; Mexican Fan Palm prevalent in California.

US.title: Country Flag
US.description: The national flag of the United States is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

US.title: Topographic Overview
US.description: The western US has major mountain ranges and high plateaus; the east is lower with the Appalachians as the main highland.

US.title: California Great Basin
US.description: Dry, shrubby valleys and tall, often snow-capped mountain ranges in eastern California near the Sierra Nevada.

US.title: California Black Stripe Between Centre Lines
US.description: A black stripe can sometimes be seen between the two yellow centre lines on California roads.

US.title: Rocky Mountains
US.description: Jagged, rocky formations from the Canadian border to northern New Mexico, often with pine forests and snow on high peaks.

US.title: Idaho Great Basin
US.description: Greener dry plains with patches of grass and shrubs, and occasional low mountain ranges.

US.title: Speed signs
US.description: Speed signs in the US say ‘Speed Limit’.

US.title: Missing Front Plates
US.description: About 22 states require only a rear plate; vehicles without front plates likely come from these states.

US.title: Red Metal Rooftops
US.description: Red metal roofs are a common sight in the southeastern U.S.

US.title: Appalachian Mountains
US.description: A low mountain range in the eastern US, covered in forest with beech and oak trees.

US.title: Thick Yellow Centre Lines, WV, VA, MD
US.description: Some roads in West Virginia, Virginia, and Maryland have centre yellow lines that are noticeably thicker than standard.

US.title: Long-Nose Semi-Trucks
US.description: North American semi-trucks have a long nose with the engine ahead of the cab.

US.title: Utah Great Basin
US.description: Dry, open plains with scattered sagebrush and distant high mountain ranges in western and central Utah.

US.title: Green Highway Exit Signs
US.description: Large green signs with white text mark exits and distances on US highways.

CO.title: Afro-Colombian Pacific Coast
CO.description: The Pacific coastline has a predominantly Afro-Colombian population.

CO.title: Concrete and Dark Poles
CO.description: Most poles are concrete, with dark-coloured poles more common here than nearby countries.

CO.title: Yellow plates
CO.description: Colombia is the only country in South America that uses all yellow license plates for personal vehicles.

CO.title: Rickety fences
CO.description: It is common to find wooden fences in Colombia, often made from various pieces of wood.

CO.title: Painted poles
CO.description: Colombian poles can be found painted with black-yellow-black stripes.

CO.title: Taxi
CO.description: Taxi cars will often feature useful information such as the name of the city they are driving in.

KZ.title: Blue Street Signs on Buildings
KZ.description: Kazakh street signs are blue with white patterns, mounted on building facades, often bilingual or trilingual.

KZ.title: Tree trunks
KZ.description: The bottom of tree trunks in Kazakhstan are often painted white.

RO.title: Licence Plates

RO.title: Romanian Language
RO.description: A Romance language with unique diacritics Ă/ă, Ș/ș, and Ț/ț.

RO.title: Country Flag
RO.description: The national flag of Romania is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

RO.title: Holey poles
RO.description: In Romania, you will frequently come across so called holey poles, with holes running all the way down to the ground.

AT.title: Licence Plates
AT.description: Austrian licence plates are elongated and white, featuring the blue EU band on the left edge.

AT.title: Anfang/Ende Signs
AT.description: Parking restriction signs often include 'Anfang' (start) or 'Ende' (end) to mark zone boundaries.

AT.title: Mountainous south
AT.description: The centre and west are mountainous, while the east and north are flatter, with rolling hills.

AT.title: Vorarlberg White Km Markers
AT.description: White kilometre markers appear in Vorarlberg and western Salzburg.

AT.title: Highest Alps
AT.description: Austria's highest Alpine peaks cluster near the Italian border in the west.

AT.title: Landscape
AT.description: Most of Austria is forested mountain terrain, with eastern regions flattening into agricultural lowlands.

AT.title: Alpine Architecture
AT.description: Traditional Alpine homes have pale walls, wooden balconies, and wide overhanging dark timber roofs.

AT.title: German Language
AT.description: Austria's official language is German, recognizable by characters Ä, Ö, Ü, and ß.

AT.title: Black top bollards
AT.description: Austrian roadside bollards are white with a black cap, often with a small rounded knob at the very top.

AT.title: Wooden Poles
AT.description: The predominant utility pole across Austria is a rounded timber design.

ZA.title: Dry Northeast Landscape
ZA.description: Arid terrain with orange-red soil and shrub-covered hills or mountains characterises the northeast.

ZA.title: Bird Poles
ZA.description: South African poles often have 1–5 horizontal bars with thin white insulators resembling rows of perching birds.

ZA.title: Triangular Warning Signs
ZA.description: South African warning signs are red-bordered triangles on a white background.

ZA.title: South African chevrons
ZA.description: South Africa uses red and white chevron signs, and small, thin chevrons with a single arrow are common across Southern African countries.

ZA.title: High security
ZA.description: In South Africa, suburban homes in and around major cities are commonly enclosed behind tall walls, fences, and gates.

ZA.title: Yellow Edge Lines
ZA.description: Most South African roads feature single yellow edge lines paired with white centre lines.

ZA.title: Green directional signs
ZA.description: South African directional signs are green with yellow road numbers. Road-numbers starting with N or R are exclusive to South Africa.

ZA.title: Afrikaans
ZA.description: South Africa has eleven official languages. While English dominates signage, the Dutch-like language Afrikaans has had a big influence on for example city names.

NO.title: Wooden Houses
NO.description: Norwegian homes are mostly wooden, often red-painted; black-painted houses are more common here than in neighbors.

NO.title: Spruce Trees
NO.description: Spruce trees are concentrated in the southern half of Norway, especially in the southeast and Trondheim region.

NO.title: Directional signs
NO.description: In Norway directional signs are yellow with a thin black outline.

NO.title: Country Flag
NO.description: The national flag of Norway is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

NO.title: White signs
NO.description: Regulatory traffic signs in Norway feature a red border on a white background.

NO.title: Coastal Grasslands
NO.description: Roads along the far northern coast pass through open grasslands with minimal vegetation and low, distant mountains.

NO.title: Beautiful views
NO.description: Fjords are a common sight along the Norwegian coast.

LK.title: Wet Southwest Climate
LK.description: The southwest receives more rainfall, producing dense, deep-green vegetation.

LK.title: Sri Lanka poles
LK.description: Sri Lanka commonly uses concrete utility poles with large see through holes in the lower half, often called holey poles

LK.title: Tuk-Tuks
LK.description: Sri Lankan tuk-tuks are bulky with a black roof, typically painted green, yellow, or red.

LK.title: Sinhala writing
LK.description: The written Sri Lankan language Sinhala have letters that are very round. Some letter makes it look like there are small doodle characters among us.

LK.title: Driving direction
LK.description: In Sri Lanka they drive on the left side of the road.

LK.title: White and yellow
LK.description: Sri Lankan license plates are white in the front and yellow in the rear.

EE.title: Architecture
EE.description: Estonian buildings combine wooden cladding, white-rendered brick, and steep corrugated metal roofs.

EE.title: Short-Dash Edge Lines
EE.description: Road edge markings sometimes use unusually short dashes.

EE.title: Estonian bollard
EE.description: Estonian bollards have a rounded profile. The front carries a rectangular reflector while the back has two circular ones, in either white or orange.

PL.title: Tree-Lined Roads
PL.description: Rows of mature trees flanking both sides of roads are common across Poland.

PL.title: Architecture
PL.description: Central European style with plain stone walls, pastel stucco, and orange, red, black, or brown roof tiles; detached homes and communist-era blocks.

PL.title: Polish Language
PL.description: A West Slavic language with unique diacritics like Ł, Ą, Ę, Ż, and Ń, and W replacing V.

PL.title: Double White Centre Lines
PL.description: All road markings are white in Poland. Double centre lines are extremely common.

PL.title: Roadside Christian Shrines
PL.description: Small roadside shrines and blue-white or yellow-white Catholic flags are frequent.

PL.title: White Prohibitory Signs
PL.description: Polish round prohibitory signs use a white background with a thicker red border.

PL.title: Country Flag
PL.description: The national flag of Poland is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

PL.title: No zebra
PL.description: Pedestrian crossing signs in Poland only features a horizontal line. No "zebra stripes" here.

PL.title: Licence Plates
PL.description: Polish plates are long and white with the standard EU blue strip on the left.

PL.title: Flat Green Landscape
PL.description: Poland features flat terrain with gentle hills, extensive agriculture, and moderate forest cover.

PL.title: Holy poles
PL.description: The utility poles in Poland are often thin and features a lot of holes. These holes usually don't go all the way down.

PL.title: Warning signs
PL.description: Poland's warning signs are triangular with a yellow background and a thin red border.

VN.title: Flat Agricultural Deltas
VN.description: Wide open, flat agricultural fields are most common in the Red River Delta and less so in the Mekong Delta.

VN.title: Mekong Delta, Low Single-Storey Houses
VN.description: Mekong Delta houses are boxy concrete and almost always single ground-level storey.

VN.title: Country Flag
VN.description: The national flag of Vietnam is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

VN.title: Central Highlands Landscape
VN.description: The Central Highlands are hilly with distant mountains, red soil, and dry rolling farmland.

VN.title: Red-and-White Striped Signposts
VN.description: Vietnamese road sign posts are usually painted with red-and-white stripes.

VN.title: Holey Concrete Poles
VN.description: Concrete poles with rows of holes, on the lower half or nearly to the top, are common in Vietnam.

VN.title: Double Poles
VN.description: Double utility poles of various designs are fairly common in Vietnam.

VN.title: Hoi An Yellow Buildings
VN.description: Hoi An is identifiable by old yellow buildings with dark brown doors and details.

VN.title: Concrete bollards
VN.description: Small concrete bollards are the most common ones in Vietnam. They have a red top.

VN.title: Vietnamese language
VN.description: The Vietnamese language is written in a modified Latin script that features an extensive system of diacritical marks.

VN.title: Waystones with Coloured Tops
VN.description: Vietnamese waystones are white with red or blue tops, showing road numbers and distances.

VN.title: Electricity boxes
VN.description: Grey electricity boxes can be seen mounted to utility poles in Vietnam. They are tapered towards the bottom and have a few windows.

VN.title: Concrete Block Roads
VN.description: Minor Vietnamese roads are often made of concrete blocks.

VN.title: Yellow-Orange Road Signs
VN.description: Vietnamese road signs have a yellow-orange background.

VN.title: Short Yellow Centre Dashes
VN.description: Short yellow dashes as centre road lines are common and distinctive in Vietnam.

PE.title: Striped signposts
PE.description: Many signposts in Peru are square-shaped and painted in alternating black and white.

PE.title: Semi-Arid Mountain Landscape
PE.description: Much of Peru has dry mountain ranges and valleys with sparse vegetation.

PE.title: Political Party Logos
PE.description: Peruvian political party logos are often painted on walls and buildings.

PE.title: Rocky Outcrops in the Central Highlands
PE.description: Exposed rock faces are common on hillsides in central Peru from Lago Chinchaycocha south to Ayacucho.

PE.title: Jagged Mountain Peaks
PE.description: Tall, sharp rocky peaks are typical from Huaraz south to Cusco, away from the coast.

PE.title: Dark Red Soil
PE.description: Reddish-tinted earth appears notably around Cusco, Ayacucho, Cajamarca, and Tarapoto.

PE.title: Road Line Markings
PE.description: Peruvian outer road lines are always white. Highways have single or double yellow centre lines. Rural mountain roads often lack a centre line.

PE.title: Licence Plates
PE.description: Peruvian plates are white or yellow; taxis have split-coloured plates, yellow on top and white on bottom.

PE.title: Red-and-White Vehicle Stickers
PE.description: Wide red-and-white reflective stickers are common on taxis and commercial vehicles in Peru.

PE.title: Southwestern Piura, Dry Flat Terrain
PE.description: Southwest of Piura is dry, sparsely vegetated, mostly flat with gentle hills.

PE.title: Tuk tuks
PE.description: Tuk Tuks are a common sight in Peru. They are usually referred to as mototaxi.

PE.title: Flat Highland Plateaus
PE.description: Flat high-altitude terrain appears in central Puno and around Lake Chinchaycocha.

FR.title: Stone Pines
FR.description: Umbrella-shaped stone pines line many roads along the Mediterranean coast, sometimes as far north as Nantes.

FR.title: Licence Plates
FR.description: Modern French plates are white rectangles with blue bands on left and right edges.

FR.title: Road Sign Borders
FR.description: Regulatory signs have a red border with a narrow white outline; white sub-signs with black text often attached below.

FR.title: Architecture
FR.description: Typical French houses are stone, unpainted or pale pastel, with simple gable roofs of orange tiles or dark slate; urban terraced houses line roads.

FR.title: Blue House Numbers
FR.description: Address plaques are predominantly blue with serif typeface and ornate numerals.

FR.title: French Car Brands
FR.description: Peugeot, Renault, and Citroën make up roughly half of all vehicles on the road.

FR.title: Black Shingle Roofs
FR.description: Slate or dark shingle roofs dominate northwest of the Loire, near the Belgian border, south-centre, and the Pyrenees.

FR.title: Topography
FR.description: Highest peaks are in the southeast (Alps) and along the Spanish border (Pyrenees). North and Atlantic coast are flat to rolling; southern interior is hillier.

FR.title: Telephone Area Codes
FR.description: Phone numbers are ten digits; first pairs indicate broad zones, with 06–09 for mobile and non-regional.

PH.title: Red-on-White Chevron Signs
PH.description: Philippine road curve chevrons use red arrows on white backgrounds.

PH.title: Tricycles / Tuk-Tuks
PH.description: Motorised tricycles (tuk-tuks) are ubiquitous and often outnumber cars.

PH.title: Concrete roads
PH.description: Roads in the Philippines are often made of big concrete blocks.

PH.title: City abbreviations
PH.description: In the Philippines city abbreviations can often be found on boxes mounted on utility poles.

PH.title: English
PH.description: English is one of the official languages in the Philippines and appears on signs frequently.

PH.title: Colourful Sign Posts
PH.description: Posts supporting road signs are frequently painted red, orange, or yellow.

PH.title: Grain Drying on Roads
PH.description: Harvested grain is often spread out on roads for drying.

PH.title: Chile-Style Indented Concrete Poles
PH.description: Square concrete utility poles with a visible indent on each side are found mainly north of Manila and around Bacolod on Negros.

PH.title: Amakan Walls with Diamond Pattern
PH.description: Houses with woven bamboo walls in a diamond pattern are found almost exclusively in the southern half of the Philippines.

PH.title: Driving direction
PH.description: They drive on the right side of the road in the Philippines.

IT.title: Architecture
IT.description: Pastel stone houses with terracotta roofs and outward-swinging bi-fold wooden shutters.

IT.title: Country Flag
IT.description: The national flag of Italy is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

IT.title: Street names
IT.description: The Italian word for street is 'Via'.

IT.title: Double stripes
IT.description: The Italian license plates will have a blue strip on both sides. The front plates are also shorter than usual.

TR.title: Ladder and Mesh Metal Poles
TR.description: Metal utility poles with ladder or mesh-grid patterns are widespread in Turkey.

TR.title: Varied Landscape Across Regions
TR.description: Turkey's terrain ranges from arid southeast plains to Mediterranean coasts and greener northern forests.

TR.title: Northeastern Treeless Grassland Valleys
TR.description: The northeast has open valleys of grass between rounded, treeless hills.

TR.title: Red-on-White Chevron Signs
TR.description: Turkish chevron signs are red arrows on a white background, often with a neon yellow border.

TR.title: Wide-Spaced Font on Direction Signs
TR.description: Turkish directional signs use a typeface with large gaps between letters.

TR.title: Grainy roads
TR.description: Many roads in Turkey have a grainy look from the mix of light and dark local stones used in the asphalt.

TR.title: Interlocking Brick Pavements
TR.description: Sidewalks and pedestrian areas often use interlocking bricks in a repeating shape.

TR.title: Metal Roofs in the East
TR.description: Sheet metal roofing is common in eastern Turkey.

SE.title: Landscape Overview
SE.description: Sweden has boreal forests, farmlands, lakes, mountainous north and west, and flatter south and east.

SE.title: White Road Lines
SE.description: All road markings in Sweden are white.

SE.title: Short dashes
SE.description: In Sweden, the outer road lines often have short, white dashed markings.

SE.title: Striped Signpost Markings
SE.description: Swedish signposts often have coloured striped markings, commonly blue-and-white or red-and-yellow.

SE.title: Red-and-Yellow Road Infrastructure
SE.description: Road infrastructure and work signs in Sweden are often painted red and yellow.

SE.title: Street Name Suffixes
SE.description: Swedish street names often end in "vägen" or "gatan," abbreviated as "v" and "g" on signs.

SE.title: Birch Rows Along the North Coast
SE.description: Long rows of thin birch trees line urban streets in northern coastal towns.

SE.title: Snow poles
SE.description: Swedish snow poles are typically orange with a tall white reflector positioned slightly above the midpoint.

SE.title: Swedish Language
SE.description: Swedish is a North Germanic language with the letters Å, Ä, and Ö.

SE.title: Broad-Leafed Trees
SE.description: Broad-leafed trees grow naturally only in southern Sweden and increase further south.

SE.title: Directional Signs
SE.description: Most Swedish directional signs are blue with white text and an arrow, while yellow signs with black text are typically used for smaller local destinations.

SE.title: Lake Mälaren Landscape
SE.description: Around Lake Mälaren, flat terrain has medium fields, forests in the background, and small tree clusters in fields.

SE.title: Place Name Endings
SE.description: Certain place name suffixes are region-specific, useful for pinpointing locations.

SE.title: Red houses
SE.description: In the countryside Sweden, along with Norway and Finland, has many of these distinct red houses with white trim.

SE.title: Light-Coloured Houses on the West Coast
SE.description: The west coast has many white and light yellow houses, especially between Gothenburg and Norway.

BO.title: Altiplano
BO.description: A highland plateau with grasslands ranging from green to brown, often with clumpy tufted grass.

BO.title: Utility Poles
BO.description: Main poles are cylindrical concrete with pinholes or timber, with varied crossarm designs.

BO.title: Red bricks
BO.description: Buildings featuring big exposed red bricks is a common sight in Bolivia.

BO.title: Tigo Telecom Branding
BO.description: Tigo's blue logo appears frequently in Bolivian urban areas.

BO.title: Road Line Colours
BO.description: Centre road markings vary between solid yellow, mixed yellow and white, or solid white; edge lines are always white.

IE.title: Diamond-Shaped Warning Signs
IE.description: Irish hazard warnings use yellow diamond-shaped boards, unique in Europe.

IE.title: Irish plates
IE.description: Irish license plates are white and have the standard EU blue strip on the left.

IE.title: Bilingual signs
IE.description: Irish road signs usually carry text in both English and Irish.

IE.title: Green Hedgerow Landscape
IE.description: Lush farmland bordered by dense hedgerows dominates the country.

IE.title: Architecture
IE.description: Rural houses are cream with dark slate roofs; urban streets have terraced row houses.

IE.title: Rounded-Corner Farm Gates
IE.description: Metal field gates almost always have rounded top corners.

IE.title: Dashed outer lines
IE.description: Irish roads often have dashed yellow outlines.

NA.title: Arid Mountains in the West and South
NA.description: Western and southern Namibia have barren, dry mountains and rocky hills.

NA.title: Desert landscape
NA.description: Desert-like landscape dominates most of Namibia, although there are a few exceptions to this.

NA.title: White truck
NA.description: Namibian Street View coverage was captured using a white pickup truck equipped with a short front-mounted antenna that consistently tilts slightly to the left.

NL.title: Brick Architecture
NL.description: Buildings are mostly red-brown brick with roofs of orange or dark grey tiles.

NL.title: Super flat
NL.description: The Netherlands is a very flat country. You won't find many hills here.

NL.title: Yellow plates
NL.description: In the Netherlands license plates are yellow, quite a rare sight in Europe.

NL.title: Brick roads
NL.description: Brick roads are common throughout the Netherlands.

NL.title: Dutch Language
NL.description: Dutch is a Germanic language with frequent double vowels and distinctive letter combinations like 'ij'.

NL.title: Striped Road Barriers
NL.description: Red-and-white striped barriers are common along Dutch roads, especially rural areas.

NL.title: All-White Road Markings
NL.description: Dutch road lines are entirely white, with common dashed edge lines and occasional green centre lines.

AD.title: Mountains all around
AD.description: Andorra is located in a mountain range between France and Spain, this leads to mountains being visible at all times.

AD.title: Stone buildings
AD.description: Stone buildings are common all across Andorra.

CL.title: Atacama and Coquimbo Mountains
CL.description: Jagged, uneven rock formations dominate Atacama and northern Coquimbo.

CL.title: Yellow or white lines
CL.description: Chile can have either fully yellow or fully white lines. The two colors are almost never combined.

CL.title: Concrete poles
CL.description: You will find rectangular, indented concrete poles in Chile. The upper part typically has small pinholes.

BD.title: Tin Roofs
BD.description: Corrugated metal roofing is widespread on residential buildings.

BD.title: Bengali language
BD.description: Bengali is an official language of Bangladesh, and its script has a horizontal line across the top of each word.

BD.title: Mid-Growth Rice
BD.description: Medium-height green rice indicates mid-season growth in Rangpur, Barishal, and Chittagong.

BD.title: White-Painted Tree Trunks
BD.description: Roads are often lined with trees whose lower trunks are painted white.

BD.title: Licence Plates
BD.description: Vehicles in Bangladesh have licence plates in white, black, or turquoise.

BD.title: Triangular letters
BD.description: Bengali, the language in Bangladesh has got a lot of triangular shapes, something similar scripts do not feature.

SI.title: Alpine architecture
SI.description: Slovenian buildings are alpine-inspired with light-colored walls and dark wooden details.

GR.title: Red Soil
GR.description: Exposed red-tinted earth is widespread in the landscape.

GR.title: Western Mountains
GR.description: Highest peaks and most high-altitude roads are in the western mainland.

GR.title: Greek Alphabet
GR.description: Greek is written in its distinctive script with rounder, softer lowercase forms.

GR.title: Mediterranean Architecture
GR.description: Stone buildings with white or pastel walls and orange tile roofs; islands feature white walls with blue doors and windows.

GR.title: Greek plates
GR.description: Greek license plates are either fully white or follow the standard EU layout with a blue strip on the left side.

GR.title: Wooden poles
GR.description: Most Greek utility poles are made of timber, often seen in a dark brown tone.

SK.title: Slovak vs Czech Language Differences
SK.description: Slovak uses unique accented letters like L with caron (Ľ) and O with circumflex (Ô); Czech uses others like R with caron (Ř) and U with ring (Ů).

SK.title: Spring Coverage
SK.description: Most imagery was captured in spring.

SK.title: Inverted Triangle Pole Supports
SK.description: Two angled braces create upside-down triangle silhouette.

NZ.title: Tightly Spaced Wooden Fence Posts
NZ.description: Wooden fences with closely packed posts are prevalent on the North Island, northern South Island, and around Akaroa.

NZ.title: Blue Street Signs
NZ.description: New Zealand street signs are predominantly blue with white text, especially in rural areas.

NZ.title: Road Line Markings
NZ.description: NZ outer road lines are generally white; centre lines are single white dashes or solid double yellow lines.

NZ.title: Intersection triangles
NZ.description: Triangles can be found painted on the road at intersections in New Zealand.

NZ.title: Licence Plates
NZ.description: New Zealand plates are white with black lettering, appearing almost entirely white when blurred.

NZ.title: Red text
NZ.description: In New Zealand, Give Way signs feature red text and a small white outline.

NZ.title: Concrete Utility Poles with Single Groove
NZ.description: NZ's main poles are concrete with a single long vertical groove and small silver possum guards.

NZ.title: Square Concrete Poles without Groove
NZ.description: Square-profile concrete poles lacking vertical grooves are most common in Southland.

NZ.title: Off-Centre Crossbars on Poles
NZ.description: Utility poles with uneven, asymmetrical crossbars appear in Otago, Marlborough, Wellington, and Taranaki.

NZ.title: Long Black Vertical Sticker (6 Digits with Square)
NZ.description: Tall black vertical stickers with six digits and a small black square appear across much of the North Island and in Southland and Otago.

NZ.title: State Highway Numbering System
NZ.description: New Zealand's two-digit state highway numbers run north to south sequentially.

NZ.title: White Sign Posts
NZ.description: NZ directional and warning signs are typically mounted on white posts; warning signs are yellow diamonds.

NZ.title: Green Directional Signs
NZ.description: New Zealand highway direction signs are green with state highway numbers inside a red shield.

NZ.title: Ferns in Forested Areas
NZ.description: Ferns are very common in New Zealand's wooded and forested areas.

NZ.title: Waikato and Northland Landscape
NZ.description: These regions feature dry conditions and rolling hills; Northland is notably hilly.

NZ.title: Very Tall Hedges in Bay of Plenty
NZ.description: Exceptionally tall hedges are characteristic around Tauranga in the Bay of Plenty.

NZ.title: Fruit Farms with Green Netting
NZ.description: Orchards draped in green protective netting are especially common around Tauranga and occasionally near Gisborne.

ES.title: Flat Signposts
ES.description: Nearly all traffic signs, kilometre markers, and chevrons are mounted on flat-profile signposts.

ES.title: Spanish Language
ES.description: Spanish is dominant; the letter Ñ is exclusive to Spanish.

ES.title: Landscape Diversity
ES.description: Spain's scenery ranges from lush forests and plateaus to semi-deserts and mountains.

ES.title: Mediterranean Climate
ES.description: Most of the country has a dry Mediterranean climate reflected in vegetation and agriculture.

ES.title: Spanish chevrons
ES.description: In Spain, you can find both black and white chevrons and blue and white chevrons.

ES.title: Canary Islands Landscapes
ES.description: Diverse landscapes: volcanic mountains, pine forests, lava fields, arid zones, and Mediterranean-like countryside.

ES.title: Lanzarote Volcanic Soil
ES.description: Very dark exposed volcanic terrain, almost lunar in places, is more abundant on Lanzarote than on any other Canary Island.

ES.title: Lanzarote Wine Plantations
ES.description: Unique vineyards where each vine is sheltered inside a semicircular stone wall built on dark volcanic soil.

ES.title: Ladder Poles and Wooden Poles
ES.description: Common poles include concrete 'ladder' poles with step-like indentations and plain wooden poles.

ES.title: Balearic Islands Landscape
ES.description: Coastal Mediterranean feel with dry Aleppo pine forests on hillsides and small agricultural patches of fruit and olive trees.

ES.title: Balearic Rock Walls
ES.description: Low dry-stone walls are extremely prevalent throughout the Balearic Islands.

ES.title: Castilla y León Flatlands
ES.description: Broad, gently undulating agricultural plain dominated by cereal crops and occasional sunflower fields.

ES.title: Baltic Pines
ES.description: Pinus sylvestris grows tall and slender with dark bark that sheds near the top to reveal orange-red wood. The lower trunk is usually branchless. Found mainly in the Pyrenees, Sierra de Guadarrama, and the Iberian System.

ES.title: Maritime Pines (Atlantic)
ES.description: Near the Atlantic coast, Pinus pinaster shows grey bark with red undertones and fluffy upward-pointing branches. Mature trees lose their lower branches.

ES.title: Maritime Pines (Mediterranean)
ES.description: Away from the Atlantic, Pinus pinaster has grey, deeply fissured bark with red tones. Found in mountain ranges across central and southern Spain.

ES.title: Green Northern Coast
ES.description: The far north is lush with rolling hills, hedgerows, and verdant meadows.

ES.title: Pyrenean Pine Forests
ES.description: Dense tall pine forests cover much of the Pyrenees and smaller hills in the Basque Country or Navarre.

ES.title: Many stripes
ES.description: On the Spanish crossing signs there are eight stripes, the most in all of Europe.

FI.title: Wooden Utility Poles
FI.description: Plain timber poles with various top fittings; street lights often mounted directly on them.

FI.title: Boreal Forests
FI.description: Thick coniferous forests dominated by pine and spruce, with birch trees having bright white bark.

FI.title: Middle Road Lines
FI.description: Centre lines appear as white dashes, solid white, solid yellow, or double yellow lines.

FI.title: Snow poles
FI.description: Finland has orange snow poles with a single narrow white band positioned close to the top.

FI.title: Red houses
FI.description: Along Sweden and Norway, Finland has many of these distinct red houses with white trim.

FI.title: Lakes
FI.description: Finland has many lakes appearing frequently across the landscape.

FI.title: Finnish Language
FI.description: Finnish has long words, frequent double vowels, and special characters ä and ö.

FI.title: Shorter plates
FI.description: In Finland, license plates are slightly shorter than in most other European countries, and they include the standard EU blue strip on the left.

FI.title: Crossing signs
FI.description: Finnish pedestrian crossing signs feature five black stripes.

CH.title: Direction Signs
CH.description: Sign colour signals road class: blue for main roads, white for secondary roads.

CH.title: Framed Signs
CH.description: In Switzerland, many road signs have a thin metal border that gives them a clean, framed look.

MX.title: Rooftop Water Tanks
MX.description: Wide cylindrical water tanks, usually black or white, are common on Mexican rooftops.

MX.title: American Car Brands and Pickup Trucks
MX.description: US vehicle brands and pickup trucks are very popular on Mexican roads.

MX.title: Octagonal poles
MX.description: Mexico usually has octagonal utility poles made of concrete.

MX.title: Electricity meters
MX.description: Mexico, along with several Central American countries, uses circular electricity meters.

MX.title: Hanging Insulators on Concrete Poles
MX.description: Concrete power poles with insulators hanging below the crossbar are typical of the Yucatan peninsula.

MX.title: Pulque Agaves
MX.description: Agave salmiana has broad, smooth, curling leaves forming a crown-like silhouette, thriving in the central valley and around San Luis Potosi.

MX.title: Irregular Cobblestone Pavement
MX.description: Streets paved with randomly arranged, irregular cobblestones are widespread in central Mexico, especially Nayarit, Jalisco, Colima, and Queretaro.

MX.title: Yellow-Painted Kerbs and Barriers
MX.description: Kerbs and bridge barriers are frequently painted yellow in Mexico.

MX.title: Golden Roadside Grass Tufts
MX.description: Lines of golden grass tufts growing immediately beside roads in Coahuila.

TH.title: Rice Cultivation Zone
TH.description: Most of Thailand's rice farming takes place within the highlighted region.

TH.title: Utility Poles
TH.description: Thai utility poles are square-profiled concrete with a vertical row of small pinholes up the shaft.

TH.title: Small circles
TH.description: In the written Thai language there is a lot of small circles on the letters.

TH.title: Directional Road Signs
TH.description: Minor-road directional signs are white with two stacked panels; highways have green signs often with romanised names.

TH.title: Concrete Roads
TH.description: Paved concrete surfaces in Thailand typically display a large square-tile pattern.

TH.title: Yellow Centre Lines
TH.description: Thai road centre markings are yellow, either solid or dashed lines.

TH.title: Overhanging Lamp Posts
TH.description: Thai lamp posts are long and slender, arcing outward over the roadway.

TH.title: Driving direction
TH.description: In Thailand they drive on the left side of the road.

TH.title: Garuda Road Markers
TH.description: Thai route-number markers feature a white or black Garuda symbol; national routes are white-and-black shields, provincial routes blue-and-yellow.

DK.title: Flat landscape
DK.description: The terrain across Denmark is predominantly flat.

DK.title: Licence Plates
DK.description: Danish plates: standard white with blue EU band, yellow for commercial vehicles, and unique 'Parrot' variant with yellow left section.

DK.title: Red-and-White Chevrons
DK.description: Curve warning boards in Denmark are red and white and tend to be positioned close to the ground.

DK.title: Roadside Bicycle Paths
DK.description: Dedicated cycle lanes running alongside the carriageway are a frequent feature of Danish roads.

DK.title: Danish Language
DK.description: Danish is a North Germanic language with letters Æ, Ø, and Å.

DK.title: Country Flag
DK.description: The national flag of Denmark is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

BG.title: Licence Plates
BG.description: Bulgarian plates have a blue EU band on the left side.

BG.title: Orange Roof Tiles
BG.description: Houses have orange clay tile roofs with visible mortar patches and uneven tilework.

BG.title: Concrete Utility Poles
BG.description: Dominant poles are round concrete cylinders.

BG.title: Metal waste bins
BG.description: It is common to spot these metal waste bins in Bulgaria.

AE.title: Arabic and English
AE.description: Signage in the UAE is bilingual, with Arabic script alongside English.

AE.title: UAE flag
AE.description: Horizontal stripes of green, white, and black with a vertical red band on the left.

AE.title: Unpaved roads
AE.description: Despite the country's wealth, it is not unusual to encounter unpaved roads in residential areas.

MK.title: Red block
MK.description: North Macedonian plates are white and can have the blue EU strip. A noticeable red block sits near the left side.

TW.title: Architecture
TW.description: Taiwanese residential buildings range from cramped multi-storey to flat single-storey homes, often boxy with white tile walls and light-green tin sheds.

TW.title: Central-Eastern Mountains
TW.description: Forested mountains cover two-thirds of Taiwan with temperate or coniferous trees at higher elevations.

TW.title: Double Yellow Centre Lines
TW.description: Most Taiwanese roads have double yellow centre lines with single white edge lines.

TW.title: Concrete Drainage Ditches
TW.description: Open concrete drainage channels run alongside many Taiwanese roads.

TW.title: Traditional Chinese
TW.description: Taiwanese signage uses Traditional Chinese, a complex script with intricate multi-stroke characters.

TW.title: Pole markings
TW.description: In Taiwan, nearly all utility poles carry diagonal black-and-yellow striped markings that most often run all the way down to the ground.
